title.zh: 卷一百〇六 列傳第四十四: 張暐子:行簡 賈益謙 劉炳 朮虎高琪 移剌塔不也
title.en: Volume 106 Biographies 44: Zhang Wei son: Xingjian, Jia Yiqian, Liu Bing, Pai Hugaoqi, Yi Latabuye
title.raw: 卷一百〇六 列傳第四十四: 張暐子:行簡 賈益謙 劉炳 朮虎高琪 移剌塔不也 Volume 106 Biographies 44: Zhang Wei son: Xingjian, Jia Yiqian, Liu Bing, Pai Hugaoqi, Yi Latabuye

sentences.zh: 張暐，字明仲，莒州日照縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, styled Mingzhong, was a man of Rizhao County in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, whose style name was Mingzhong, came from Rizhao County in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 博學該通。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and comprehensively versed.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply learned and masterful across many fields.

sentences.zh: 登正隆五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Zhenglong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhenglong reign he qualified as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 調陳留主簿、淄州酒稅副使，課增羨，遷昌樂令。

translations.literal: He was assigned as Chief Clerk of Chenliu and Deputy Commissioner of Wine Taxes in Zizhou; because tax receipts increased with surplus, he was transferred to Magistrate of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as chief clerk of Chenliu and deputy commissioner of wine taxes in Zizhou; when collections rose well above quota, he was promoted to magistrate of Changle.

sentences.zh: 改永清令，補尚書省令史，除太常博士，兼國子助教。

translations.literal: He was changed to Magistrate of Yongqing, supplemented as a clerk in the Department of State Affairs, appointed Grand Master of Sacrifices in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and concurrently served as Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as magistrate of Yongqing, then filled a clerkship in the Department of State Affairs, was appointed grand master of sacrifices in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and also served as assistant instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，調山東東路轉運副使，入為太常丞，兼左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning; when mourning ended, he was assigned Deputy Transport Commissioner of Shandong East Circuit, entered the capital as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and concurrently served as Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning, and when the mourning period ended he was made deputy transport commissioner of the Shandong East Circuit. He then entered the capital as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently served as left mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 章宗封原王，兼原王府文學。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuan, Wei concurrently served as Literary Instructor in the Yuan Prince's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuan, Wei also served as literary instructor in the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 章宗冊為皇太孫，複為左贊善，轉左諭德，兼太常丞，充宋國報諭使。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong was installed as Imperial Grandson, Wei again became Left Mentor, was transferred to Left Preceptor, concurrently served as Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices, and filled the post of envoy to announce condolences to Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong was installed as imperial grandson, Wei again became left mentor, then moved to left preceptor while retaining his post as vice director of imperial sacrifices, and served as Jin envoy to announce condolences in Song.

sentences.zh: 至盱眙，宋人請赴宴，暐曰：「大行在殯，未可。」

translations.literal: When he reached Xuyi, the Song people invited him to a banquet; Wei said: "The late emperor lies in coffin—it is not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: At Xuyi the Song hosts invited him to a banquet, but Wei replied, "The late emperor still lies in state; this is not permissible."

sentences.zh: 及受賜，不舞蹈，宋人服其知禮。

translations.literal: When he received gifts, he did not perform the dance of obeisance; the Song people admired his understanding of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the imperial gifts he did not perform the ritual dance of obeisance, and the Song side respected his mastery of propriety.

sentences.zh: 使還，遷太常少卿，兼修起居注。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently compiled the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: After the embassy he was promoted to vice minister of imperial sacrifices and also joined in compiling the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 改禮部郎中，修起居注如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites, continuing to compile the Imperial Diary as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as bureau director in the Ministry of Rites while continuing his work on the imperial diary as before.

sentences.zh: 遷右諫議大夫，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Grand Master and concurrently Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right remonstrance grand master and concurrently served as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，太傅徒單克甯薨，章宗欲親為燒飯，是時，孝懿皇后梓宮在殯，暐奏：」仰惟聖慈，追念勳臣，恩禮隆厚，孰不感勸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang, Grand Tutor Tudan Kening died; Zhangzong wished to perform the burnt-offering meal in person; at that time Empress Dowager Xiaoyi's coffin still lay in state; Wei submitted: "Looking up to Your Sacred Kindness in recalling a meritorious minister—the gracious rites are so abundant that who would not be moved?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingchang, Grand Tutor Tudan Kening died, and Zhangzong wished to perform the funeral burnt-rice offering in person. At that time the coffin of Empress Dowager Xiaoyi still lay in state. Wei memorialized, "Your Majesty's gracious remembrance of a meritorious servant is so generous in ritual that none could fail to be stirred by it."

sentences.zh: 太祖時享，尚且權停，若為大臣燒飯，禮有未安。

translations.literal: Even the seasonal sacrifices to Taizu were for the time being suspended; if Your Majesty personally burned offerings for a minister, there would be ritual impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: Even the regular sacrifices to Taizu had been temporarily suspended; for Your Majesty to burn offerings for a minister would leave the rites unsettled.

sentences.zh: 今已降恩旨，聖意至厚，人皆知之，乞俯從典禮，則兩全矣。」

translations.literal: You have already issued a gracious edict; your intent is exceedingly generous and all know it; I beg that Your Majesty yield to established ritual—then both aims may be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Your gracious edict has already been issued, and everyone knows how deep your intent is; I beg that Your Majesty defer to established ritual so that both propriety and kindness may be preserved.

sentences.zh: 章宗從之。

translations.literal: Zhangzong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 上封事者言提刑司可罷，暐上疏曰：「陛下即位，因民所利，更法立制，無慮數十百條。

translations.literal: Someone submitting a sealed memorial said the Office of Punishment and Investigation could be abolished; Wei submitted: "Since Your Majesty's accession, reforming laws for the people's benefit—you have enacted measures beyond numbering, perhaps dozens or hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: A memorialist in a sealed report argued that the Office of Punishment and Investigation should be abolished. Wei submitted, "Since Your Majesty's accession you have reformed laws for the people's benefit, enacting reforms that must number in the dozens or hundreds.

sentences.zh: 提刑之設，政之大者，若為浮議所搖，則內外無所取信。

translations.literal: Establishing the punishment commissioners is a great matter of governance; if swayed by loose talk, neither court nor provinces will know what to trust.
translations.idiomatic: The establishment of the punishment commissioners is a major pillar of government; if it is shaken by idle talk, neither the court nor the provinces will know what to rely on.

sentences.zh: 唐開元中，或請選擇守令，停採訪使，姚崇奏'十道採訪猶未盡得人，天下三百餘州，縣多數倍，安得守令皆稱其職？

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era of Tang, some asked to select prefects and magistrates and abolish the investigation commissioners; Yao Chong submitted: "Even the ten-circuit commissioners do not fully obtain the right men; the realm has more than three hundred prefectures and counties many times that—how can every magistrate fulfill his office?"
translations.idiomatic: In Tang's Kaiyuan reign some proposed selecting prefects and magistrates directly and abolishing the investigation commissioners. Yao Chong replied, "Even the ten-circuit investigators still fail to obtain the right men everywhere; the realm has more than three hundred prefectures and many times that number of counties—how can every prefect and magistrate fully perform his duties?"

sentences.zh: '然則提刑之任，誠不可罷，擇其人而用之，生民之大利，國家之長策也。」

translations.literal: Therefore the office of punishment commissioners truly cannot be abolished; selecting worthy men to employ them is great benefit to the people and a long-term strategy for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the post of punishment commissioner truly cannot be abolished; to choose the right men and employ them is a great benefit to the people and a lasting policy for the state."

sentences.zh: 因舉漢刺史六條以奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cited the Han six regulations for inspectors in his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited the Han dynasty's six regulations for regional inspectors in support of his memorial.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言與朕意合。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words accord with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What you say matches my own thinking."

sentences.zh: 承安元年八月壬子，上召暐至內殿，問曰：「南郊大祀，今用度不給，俟他年可乎？」

translations.literal: On renzi, eighth month, first year of Cheng'an, the emperor summoned Wei to the inner hall and asked: "For the great suburban sacrifice, present expenditures are insufficient—might we wait for another year?"
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the eighth month of the first year of Cheng'an, the emperor summoned Wei to the inner hall and asked, "Funds are insufficient for the great suburban sacrifice—might we wait until another year?"

sentences.zh: 暐曰：「陛下即位於今八年，大禮未舉，宜亟行之。」

translations.literal: Wei said: "Your Majesty has reigned eight years and the great rite has not been performed—it should be carried out promptly."
translations.idiomatic: Wei replied, "Your Majesty has reigned eight years, yet the great rite has still not been performed; it should be carried out at once."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「北方未寧，致齋之際，有不測奏報何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The north is not yet settled; during the fast, what if unexpected reports arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The north is not yet secure; during the period of purification, what if unforeseen reports should arrive?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「豈可逆度而妨大禮。

translations.literal: He replied: "How can one anticipate mishaps and obstruct the great rite?
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "How can one anticipate trouble in advance and let it obstruct the great rite?

sentences.zh: 今河平歲豐，正其時也。」

translations.literal: Now the Yellow River is calm and the harvest abundant—this is precisely the time."
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River is calm and the harvest plentiful—this is exactly the right moment."

sentences.zh: 上複問曰：「僧道三年一試，八十而取一，不亦少乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor again asked: "Monks and Daoists are tested every three years, one in eighty selected—is that not too few?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "Monks and Daoist priests are examined every three years, with only one in eighty chosen—is that not too few?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此輩浮食，無益有損，不宜滋益也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "These people live idly at others' expense; they benefit nothing and harm much—they ought not be increased."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "These people live as idle dependents; they do more harm than good and ought not be increased."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「周武帝、唐武宗、後周世宗皆賢君，其壽不永，雖曰偶然，似亦有因也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, Emperor Wuzong of Tang, and Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou were all worthy rulers, yet their lives were brief—though called coincidence, there seems to be cause."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, Emperor Wuzong of Tang, and Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou were all worthy rulers, yet none lived long. Though one may call it chance, there seems to be a reason."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「三君矯枉太過。

translations.literal: He replied: "Those three rulers corrected excess too far.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Those three rulers overcorrected when they tried to set things right.

sentences.zh: 今不毀除、不崇奉，是為得中矣。」

translations.literal: Now neither destroying nor exalting them—that is hitting the mean."
translations.idiomatic: Now, neither destroying them nor exalting them—that is the true middle course."

sentences.zh: 是歲，郊見上帝焉。

translations.literal: That year the emperor performed the suburban audience with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor carried out the suburban sacrifice and beheld Heaven.

sentences.zh: 頃之，翰林修撰路鐸論胥持國不可再用，因及董師中趨走持國及丞相襄之門，上曰：「張暐父子必不如是也。」

translations.literal: Soon Academician Compiler Lu Duo argued Xu Chiguo should not be reused, and mentioned Dong Shizhong's rushing to Xu and Chancellor Xiang's gate; the emperor said: "Zhang Wei and his sons are surely not like that."
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Hanlin academician compiler Lu Duo argued that Xu Chiguo should not be employed again and mentioned Dong Shizhong's rushing to attend upon Xu and upon Chancellor Xiang's gate. The emperor said, "Zhang Wei and his sons are surely not like that."

sentences.zh: 三年，為御史大夫，懇辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the third year he became Censor-in-Chief; he earnestly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed censor-in-chief; he earnestly declined, but the appointment was not withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐奏事不實，奪一官，解職。

translations.literal: The next year, for memorializing on affairs not truthfully, he was stripped of one rank and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, because his memorials on official business were found untrue, he was demoted one rank and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 起為安武軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Military Commissioner of Anwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled and appointed military commissioner of the Anwu Army.

sentences.zh: 致仕，例給半俸，久之，暐不復請，遂止。

translations.literal: On retirement, by regulation half salary was given; after a long time Wei no longer requested it, and it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Upon retirement he was by regulation granted half salary; after a long while Wei ceased to request it, and the payment stopped.

sentences.zh: 暐自妻卒後不復娶，亦無姬侍，齋居與子行簡講論古今，諸孫課誦其側，至夜分乃罷，以為常。

translations.literal: After his wife's death Wei did not remarry and had no concubines; in abstemious seclusion he discussed past and present with his son Xingjian, while grandsons recited lessons beside them until midnight—this was his routine.
translations.idiomatic: After his wife died Wei neither remarried nor kept concubines. Living in quiet seclusion, he discussed past and present with his son Xingjian while his grandsons recited their lessons nearby, continuing until midnight as his daily habit.

sentences.zh: 曆太常，禮部二十餘年，最明古今禮學，家法為士族儀錶。

translations.literal: Over more than twenty years in Imperial Sacrifices and Rites he was foremost in ancient and modern ritual learning; his household standards were the model for gentry clans.
translations.idiomatic: He served more than twenty years in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites and was the foremost authority on ritual learning ancient and modern; the standards of his household became the measure for the gentry.

sentences.zh: 子行簡、行信，行信自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons were Xingjian and Xingxin; Xingxin has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xingjian and Xingxin; Xingxin has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 子 行簡

translations.literal: Son: Xingjian.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zhang Xingjian.

sentences.zh: 司天臺劉道用改進新曆，詔學士院更定曆名，行簡奏乞複校測驗，俟將來月食無差，然後賜名。

translations.literal: Liu Daoyong of the Astronomical Bureau revised and presented a new calendar; an edict ordered the Academy of Scholars to fix the calendar name; Xingjian memorialized requesting re-verification and testing, waiting until a coming lunar eclipse showed no discrepancy before conferring a name.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoyong of the Directorate of Astronomy revised and presented a new calendar, and an edict ordered the Academy of Scholars to set its name. Xingjian memorialized asking that it be verified again and tested, and that a name be granted only after a coming lunar eclipse showed no error.

sentences.zh: 詔翰林侍講學士党懷英等複校。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hanlin Palace Lecturer Dang Huaiying and others to re-examine it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hanlin palace lecturer Dang Huaiying and others to re-examine the calendar.

sentences.zh: 懷英等校定道用新曆：明昌三年不置閏，即以閏月為三月；

translations.literal: Huaiying and others verified Daoyong's new calendar: in the third year of Mingchang no intercalary month was set—they simply made the intercalary month the third month;
translations.idiomatic: Huaiying and his colleagues verified Daoyong's new calendar and found that in the third year of Mingchang it omitted an intercalary month and simply treated the intercalary month as the third month;

sentences.zh: 二年十二月十四日，金木星俱在危十三度，道用曆在十三日，差一日；

translations.literal: on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month of the second year, Venus and Jupiter were both at thirteen degrees in Wei, while Daoyong's calendar placed them on the thirteenth—off by one day;
translations.idiomatic: on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month of the second year Venus and Jupiter were both at thirteen degrees in the lodge Wei, whereas Daoyong's calendar placed them on the thirteenth, a discrepancy of one day;

sentences.zh: 三年四月十六日夜月食，時刻不同。

translations.literal: on the night of the sixteenth day of the fourth month of the third year there was a lunar eclipse, but the times differed.
translations.idiomatic: and on the night of the sixteenth day of the fourth month of the third year a lunar eclipse occurred, but the predicted time did not match.

sentences.zh: 道用不會考驗古今所記，比登事蹟，輒以上進，不可用。

translations.literal: Daoyong did not know how to verify against ancient and modern records and compare with actual events—he rashly submitted it upward; it cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyong did not know how to test the calendar against ancient and modern records or compare it with observed events, yet he submitted it anyway; it cannot be adopted.

sentences.zh: 道用當徒一年收贖，長行彭徽等四人各杖八十罷去。

translations.literal: Daoyong was sentenced to one year of penal servitude redeemable by payment; Senior Clerk Peng Hui and four others were each beaten eighty strokes and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyong was sentenced to one year of penal servitude, redeemable by fine; senior clerk Peng Hui and four others were each flogged eighty strokes and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 群臣屢請上尊號，章宗不從，將下詔以示四方，行簡奏曰：「往年饑民棄子，或丐以與人，其後詔書官為收贖，或其父母衣食稍充，即識認，官亦斷與之。

translations.literal: The ministers repeatedly requested a superior honorific title; Zhangzong refused; about to issue an edict to show the realm, Xingjian memorialized: "In past years hungry people abandoned children or begged to give them away; later an edict had officials redeem them, or when parents' food and clothing improved slightly they recognized the child and officials also ruled to return him.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers repeatedly asked that a superior honorific title be granted, but Zhangzong refused. When an edict was about to be issued to announce this to the realm, Xingjian memorialized, "In earlier famine years people abandoned their children or begged others to take them. Later an edict ordered officials to redeem such children, and if the parents' food and clothing improved even slightly they would recognize the child and officials would also rule that he be returned.

sentences.zh: 自此以後，饑歲流離道路，人不肯收養，肆為捐瘠，餓死溝中。

translations.literal: Since then, in famine years those on the roads were not taken in; they wasted away and starved in ditches.
translations.idiomatic: Since then, in years of famine those wandering the roads have gone unadopted, wasting away until they starved to death in ditches.

sentences.zh: 伏見近代禦災詔書，皆曰'以後不得複取'今乞依此施行。」

translations.literal: I observe that recent disaster-relief edicts all say 'hereafter one may not reclaim'—I beg that this be applied now."
translations.idiomatic: I note that recent disaster-relief edicts all state that thereafter children may not be reclaimed; I beg that the same rule be applied in the present case."

sentences.zh: 上是其言，詔書中行之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words; the edict embodied them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his argument, and the edict carried it into effect.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼同修國史。

translations.literal: After some time, he concurrently joined in compiling the National History.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was also appointed to compile the National History.

sentences.zh: 改禮部侍郎、提點司天臺，直學士，同修史如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, Supervisor of the Astronomical Bureau, and Academician Expositor, continuing National History compilation as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as vice minister of rites and supervisor of the Directorate of Astronomy, with the rank of academician expositor, while continuing his work on the National History as before.

sentences.zh: 行簡言：「唐制，僕射、宰相上日，百官通班致賀，降階答拜。

translations.literal: Xingjian said: "Under the Tang system, when the Grand Counselor or chancellor took office, all officials offered congratulations in a single assembly, and he descended the steps to return bows.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian said, "Under the Tang system, when a grand counselor or chancellor assumed office, all officials offered congratulations in a single assembly, and he descended the steps to return their bows.

sentences.zh: 國朝皇太子元正、生日，三師、三公、宰執以下須群官同班拜賀，皇太子立受再答拜。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, on New Year's Day and the crown prince's birthday, the Three Preceptors, Three Dukes, and chancellors down must have all officials congratulate in one assembly; the crown prince stands to receive and again returns bows.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, on New Year's Day and on the crown prince's birthday, the three preceptors, three dukes, and chancellors down must join all officials in a single assembly to offer congratulations, while the crown prince stands to receive them and returns bows twice.

sentences.zh: 今尚書省宰執上日，分六品以下別為一班揖賀，宰執坐答揖，左右司郎中五品官廷揖，亦坐答之。

translations.literal: Now when chancellors of the Department of State Affairs take office, officials of the sixth rank and below are separated into another assembly to bow in congratulation; the chancellors sit and return bows with raised hands; the left and right bureau directors, fifth-rank officials, bow in the courtyard, and they also sit to return bows.
translations.idiomatic: Today, when a chancellor of the Department of State Affairs assumes office, officials of the sixth rank and below are placed in a separate assembly to bow in congratulation, while the chancellors sit and return bows with raised hands; the left and right bureau directors, fifth-rank officials, bow in the courtyard, and the chancellors again sit to return those bows.

sentences.zh: 臣謂身坐舉手答揖，近於坐受也。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that to sit and raise the hand in returning a bow is close to sitting and receiving obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that to remain seated and raise the hand in returning a bow comes too close to sitting and receiving obeisance.

sentences.zh: 宰執受賀，其禮乃重于皇太子，鞏于義未安。

translations.literal: For chancellors to receive congratulations—the rite is heavier than for the crown prince; it is rigid in ritual propriety and unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: For chancellors to receive congratulations in this way makes their ritual weightier than the crown prince's, which offends propriety and cannot be accepted.

sentences.zh: 別嫌明微，禮之大節，伏請宰執上日令三品以下官同班賀，宰執起立，依見三品官儀式通答揖。」

translations.literal: Separating suspicions and clarifying distinctions is a great point of ritual; I humbly beg that on a chancellor's first day officials of the third rank and below offer congratulations in one assembly, and the chancellors rise and return bows according to the form used when receiving third-rank officials."
translations.idiomatic: Distinguishing ranks and clarifying distinctions is a cardinal point of ritual; I humbly ask that on a chancellor's first day officials of the third rank and below offer congratulations in a single assembly, and that the chancellors rise and return bows in the manner used when receiving third-rank officials."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此事何不早辨正之，如都省擅行，卿論之是矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why was this not clarified earlier? If the chief secretariat acted on its own authority, your argument is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why was this not corrected earlier? If the chief secretariat acted on its own authority, your criticism is right."

sentences.zh: 行簡對曰：「禮部蓋嘗參酌古今典禮，擬定儀式，省廷不從，輒改以奏。」

translations.literal: Xingjian replied: "The Ministry of Rites had once weighed ancient and modern canonical rites and drafted the ceremony, but the secretariat did not follow it and altered it before submitting."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian answered, "The Ministry of Rites had already weighed ancient and modern canonical rites and drafted the proper ceremony, but the secretariat would not accept it and altered the form before submitting it."

sentences.zh: 下尚書省議，遂用之。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Department of State Affairs for deliberation, and his proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Department of State Affairs for deliberation, and his proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 宰執上日，三品以下群官通班賀，起立答拜，自此始。

translations.literal: From this time on, when chancellors took office, all officials of the third rank and below offered congratulations in one assembly, and the chancellors rose to return bows.
translations.idiomatic: From that time forward, when a chancellor assumed office, officials of the third rank and below offered congratulations in a single assembly while the chancellors rose to return bows.

sentences.zh: 行簡轉對，因論典故之學，乞于太常博士之下置檢閱官二員，通禮學資淺者使為之，積資乃遷博士。

translations.literal: In a palace audience Xingjian discussed the study of canonical precedents and requested that two review officers be placed below the grand masters of sacrifices in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices—men of shallow qualification in ritual learning should fill the posts, and after accumulating seniority they would be transferred to grand master.
translations.idiomatic: In a palace audience Xingjian spoke on the study of canonical precedents and asked that two review officers be appointed beneath the grand masters of sacrifices—men with modest grounding in ritual learning should hold the posts and, after accumulating seniority, be promoted to grand master.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今雖有《國朝集禮》，至於食貨、官職、兵刑沿革，未有成書，乞定會要，以示無窮。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Although we now have the Collected Rites of the Dynasty, as to the evolution of food and goods, offices, military affairs, and punishments, there is no completed book; I beg that an institutional compendium be fixed to show this for all time."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Although we now have the Collected Rites of the Dynasty, there is still no comprehensive book on the evolution of finance, offices, military affairs, and penal law; I beg that an institutional compendium be compiled to preserve this knowledge for posterity."

sentences.zh: 承安五年，遷侍講學士，同修史、提點司天如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Cheng'an he was promoted to Palace Lecturer Academician, continuing National History compilation and supervision of the Astronomical Bureau as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Cheng'an he was promoted to palace lecturer academician, while retaining his posts in National History compilation and supervision of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年，為宋主生日副使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he served as deputy envoy for the Song ruler's birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe he served as deputy envoy to congratulate the Song emperor on his birthday.

sentences.zh: 上召生日使完顏瑭戒之曰：「卿過界勿飲酒，每事聽于行簡。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the birthday envoy Wanyan Tang and admonished him: "When you cross the border do not drink wine; in every matter obey Xingjian."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the birthday envoy Wanyan Tang and warned him, "When you cross the border do not drink wine; in every matter defer to Xingjian."

sentences.zh: 謂行簡曰：「宋人行禮，好事末節，苟有非是，皆須正之，舊例所有，不可不至。」

translations.literal: To Xingjian he said: "The Song people observe ritual and love minor details; if anything is not correct, you must rectify it, yet whatever old precedent requires must not be neglected."
translations.idiomatic: To Xingjian he said, "The Song are punctilious in ritual and fond of minor details; if anything is improper you must correct it, yet every point required by established precedent must still be observed."

sentences.zh: 上複曰：「頗聞前奉使者過淮，每至中流，即以分界爭渡船，此殊非禮。

translations.literal: The emperor again said: "I have often heard that former envoys crossing the Huai, whenever they reached midstream, would dispute ferry boats by the boundary line—this is quite contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added, "I have often heard that previous envoys crossing the Huai would dispute ferry boats over the boundary line as soon as they reached midstream; this is wholly contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 卿自戒舟人，且語宋使曰：'兩國和好久矣，不宜爭細故傷大體。

translations.literal: You yourself must warn the boatmen, and also tell the Song envoy: 'The two states have been at peace for long; one should not quarrel over small matters and harm the larger relationship.'
translations.idiomatic: Warn your boatmen yourself, and tell the Song envoy as well, 'Our two states have been at peace for a long time; we should not quarrel over trifles and injure the larger relationship.'

sentences.zh: '丁寧諭之，使悉此意也。」

translations.literal: Urge this upon them repeatedly so that they fully understand this intent."
translations.idiomatic: Urge this upon them repeatedly so that they fully understand your meaning."

sentences.zh: 四年，詔曰：「每奏事之際，須令張行簡常在左右。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict said: "Whenever memorials are presented, Zhang Xingjian must always be at my side."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict stated, "Whenever affairs are reported to the throne, Zhang Xingjian must always remain at my side."

sentences.zh: 五年，群臣複請上尊號，上不許，詔行簡作批答，因問行簡宋范祖禹作《唐鑒》論尊號事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the ministers again requested a superior honorific title; the emperor did not consent and ordered Xingjian to draft the written reply; he then asked Xingjian about the Song scholar Fan Zuyu's discussion of honorific titles in Reflections on Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the ministers again asked that a superior honorific title be granted, but the emperor refused and ordered Xingjian to draft the written reply. He then asked Xingjian about the Song scholar Fan Zuyu's discussion of honorific titles in his Reflections on Tang.

sentences.zh: 行簡對曰：「司馬光亦嘗諫尊號事，不若祖禹之詞深至，以謂臣子生諡君父，頗似慘切。」

translations.literal: Xingjian replied: "Sima Guang also once remonstrated on honorific titles, but his words are not as profound as Zuyu's; he said that for subjects to give posthumous titles to their ruler and father seems rather painfully severe."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian answered, "Sima Guang also once remonstrated against honorific titles, but his language is not as penetrating as Fan Zuyu's. Fan argued that for subjects to bestow posthumous titles upon their living ruler and father seems almost painfully severe."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿用祖禹意答之，仍曰太祖雖有尊號，太宗未嘗受也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Use Zuyu's meaning in your reply, and also say that although Taizu received an honorific title, Taizong never accepted one."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Answer using Fan Zuyu's reasoning, and add that although Taizu received an honorific title, Taizong never accepted one."

sentences.zh: 行簡乞不拘對偶，引祖禹以微見其意。

translations.literal: Xingjian requested not to be bound by parallel prose and to cite Zuyu so as subtly to reveal the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian asked to be freed from the constraints of parallel prose and to cite Fan Zuyu so as subtly to convey the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 其文深雅，甚得代言之體。

translations.literal: The text was profound and elegant, fully attaining the style of imperial composition.
translations.idiomatic: The resulting text was refined and elegant, fully capturing the tone appropriate to imperial composition.

sentences.zh: 改順天軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of Shuntian Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as military commissioner of the Shuntian Army.

sentences.zh: 上謂行簡曰：「卿未更治民，今至保州，民之情偽，卒難臆度，如何治之則可？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Xingjian: "You have not yet governed the people; now that you are going to Baozhou, the people's true and false claims are suddenly hard to guess—how may one govern there properly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Xingjian, "You have not yet governed the people directly. Now that you are going to Baozhou, the people's true circumstances will be hard to judge at once. How should you govern there?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣奉行法令，不敢違失，獄訟之事，以情察之，鈐制公吏，禁抑豪猾，以鎮靜為務，庶幾萬分之一。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject will carry out the laws and dare not violate them; in litigation I will examine according to the facts, restrain clerks, suppress powerful bullies, and make tranquillity my task—perhaps one part in ten thousand may be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your subject will uphold the laws without deviation, examine litigation according to the facts, restrain government clerks, and suppress powerful bullies, making tranquillity my chief aim—perhaps I may succeed in some small measure."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「在任半歲或一年，所得利害上之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "After half a year or a year in office, memorialize whatever benefits or harms you have found."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "After half a year or a year in office, report whatever benefits or harms you have observed."

sentences.zh: 行簡到保州，上書曰：「比者括官田給軍，既一定矣，有告欲別給者，輒從其告，至今未已。

translations.literal: When Xingjian reached Baozhou he submitted: "Recently official fields were surveyed and allotted to the army; once this was fixed, anyone who petitioned for a separate allotment was at once granted it, and this has not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingjian reached Baozhou he memorialized, "Recently official fields were surveyed and allotted to the army. Once that allocation was settled, anyone who petitioned for a separate grant was immediately given one, and this has still not stopped.

sentences.zh: 名曰官田，實取之民以與之，奪彼與此，徒啟爭端。

translations.literal: Called official fields, in fact they are taken from the people and given to others; seizing from one to give to another only breeds disputes.
translations.idiomatic: Though called official fields, they are in fact taken from the people and given to others; seizing from one party to give to another only breeds conflict.

sentences.zh: 臣所管已撥深澤縣地三百餘頃，複告水占沙堿者三分之二，若悉從之，何時可定。

translations.literal: In the territory I administer more than three hundred qing of land in Shenze County have already been allotted; again petitions claim two-thirds are flooded, occupied by water, or saline—if all are granted, when can it be settled?
translations.idiomatic: In the territory under my administration more than three hundred qing of land in Shenze County have already been allotted, yet new petitions claim that two-thirds of it is flooded, waterlogged, or saline. If every claim is granted, when will the matter ever be settled?

sentences.zh: 臣謂當限以月日，不許再告為便。」

translations.literal: Your subject considers it best to set a limit by month and day and not permit further petitions."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes it would be best to set a deadline after which further petitions should not be accepted."

sentences.zh: 下尚書省議，奏請：「如實有水占河塌，不可耕種，本路及運司佐官按視，尚書省下按察司複同，然後改撥。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the Department of State Affairs for deliberation; they memorialized: "If there is truly water occupation or river collapse making cultivation impossible, assistant officials of the circuit and transport commission shall inspect on site, the investigation office under the Department of State Affairs shall jointly verify, and only then may reassignment be made.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Department of State Affairs, which memorialized, "If land is truly waterlogged or ruined by river collapse so that it cannot be cultivated, assistant officials of the circuit and transport commission should inspect it on site, the investigation office under the Department of State Affairs should verify jointly, and only then may the allotment be changed.

sentences.zh: 若沙堿瘠薄，當准已撥為定。」

translations.literal: If the land is saline, barren, or thin, the prior allotment should stand as fixed."
translations.idiomatic: If the land is merely saline, barren, or poor, the existing allotment should be treated as final."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可。」

translations.literal: The imperial rescript said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial rescript read, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 六年，召為禮部尚書，兼侍講、同修國史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Minister of Rites, concurrently Palace Lecturer and compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled to serve as minister of rites, while also retaining his posts as palace lecturer and compiler of the National History.

sentences.zh: 秘書監進《太一新曆》，詔行簡校之。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Library presented the Taiyi New Calendar; an edict ordered Xingjian to review it.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the Palace Library presented the Taiyi New Calendar, and an edict ordered Xingjian to review it.

sentences.zh: 七年，上遣中使馮賢童以實封禦紮賜行簡曰：「朕念鎬、鄭二王誤幹天常，自貽伊戚。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor sent the palace envoy Feng Xiantong with a sealed imperial note to bestow on Xingjian: "I recall that the Princes of Hao and Zheng offended against Heaven's constancy and brought calamity upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor sent the palace envoy Feng Xiantong with a sealed imperial note to Xingjian, saying, "I recall that the Princes of Hao and Zheng violated Heaven's order and brought ruin upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 槁葬郊野，多歷年所，朕甚悼焉。

translations.literal: They were buried withered rites in the outskirts; many years have passed, and I am deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: They were buried with scant ceremony in the open countryside, and many years have passed; I am deeply grieved by this.

sentences.zh: 欲追複前爵，備禮改葬，卿可詳閱唐貞觀追贈隱、巢，並前代故事，密封以聞。」

translations.literal: I wish to restore their former titles, provide full rites, and rebury them; you should carefully review Tang Zhenguan's posthumous enfeoffment of the Princes Yin and Chao and precedents of earlier ages, seal your report, and inform me."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to restore their former titles, provide full funeral rites, and rebury them properly. Review carefully the Tang Zhenguan precedents for posthumous enfeoffment of the Princes Yin and Chao, together with earlier models, seal your findings, and report to me."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「欲使石古乃於威州擇地營葬，歲時祭奠，兼命衛王諸子中立一人為鄭王后，謹其祭祀。

translations.literal: He also said: "I wish Shigu Nai to choose ground at Weizhou and arrange burial, with seasonal sacrifices; also appoint one of the Prince of Wei's sons, to be determined, as heir to the Prince of Zheng and carefully maintain his sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I wish Shigu Nai to choose a site at Weizhou and arrange the burial, with sacrifices at the proper seasons, and also to appoint one of the Prince of Wei's sons—whichever is suitable—as heir to the Prince of Zheng and charge him with maintaining the rites of worship.

sentences.zh: 此事既行，理須降詔，卿草詔文大意，一就封進。」

translations.literal: Once this matter is carried out, an edict must logically be issued; draft the main points of the edict text and submit it sealed in one memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Once this is carried out, an edict must naturally be issued; draft the main points of the edict and submit them together in a single sealed memorial."

sentences.zh: 行簡乃具漢淮南厲王長、楚王英、唐隱太子建成、巢剌王元吉、譙王重福故事為奏，並進詔草，遂施行焉。

translations.literal: Xingjian then set forth in a memorial the precedents of Han's Prince Li of Huainan, Liu Chang, Prince Ying of Chu, Tang's Yin Crown Prince Jiancheng, Chao Prince Yuanji, and Qiao Prince Chongfu, and together submitted the draft edict; it was thereupon carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian then compiled a memorial citing the precedents of Liu Chang, Prince Li of Huainan, Prince Ying of Chu, the Tang Yin Crown Prince Jiancheng, Prince Yuanji of Chao, and Prince Chongfu of Qiao, submitted the draft edict along with it, and the measure was carried out.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子太保、翰林學士承旨，尚書、修史如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Academician-in-Ordinary of the Hanlin Academy; his posts as Minister and compiler of history remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to grand mentor of the heir apparent and academician-in-ordinary of the Hanlin Academy, while retaining his posts as minister and compiler of the National History.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，轉太子太傅，上書論議和事，其略曰：「東海郡候嘗遣約和，較計細故，遷延不決。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyou era he was transferred to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and memorialized on the question of peace talks, in summary saying: "The Marquis of Eastern Sea Commandery once sent envoys to propose peace; we weighed petty details and delayed without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyou era he was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent and memorialized on peace negotiations, writing in summary, "The Marquis of Eastern Sea Commandery once sent envoys proposing peace, yet we haggled over petty details and delayed without reaching a decision.

sentences.zh: 今都城危急，豈可拒絕。

translations.literal: Now the capital is in grave peril—how can we refuse?
translations.idiomatic: Now the capital stands in grave peril—how can we refuse?

sentences.zh: 臣願更留聖慮，包荒含垢，以救生靈。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that Your Sagely consideration be given once more, embracing what is coarse and bearing what is filthy, to save the living people.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that Your Majesty reconsider, bearing humiliation and enduring disgrace if need be, to save the people.

sentences.zh: 或如遼、宋相為敵國，歲奉幣帛，或二三年以繼。

translations.literal: Perhaps as Liao and Song treated each other as enemy states, sending silks and cloth yearly, or continuing for two or three years.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps we might treat them as the Liao and Song once treated each other—as rival states—sending silks and cloth each year, or continuing such an arrangement for two or three years.

sentences.zh: 選忠實辨捷之人，往與議之，庶幾有成，可以紓患。」

translations.literal: Select men loyal, solid, discerning, and quick of speech to go negotiate with them; perhaps something may be achieved to relieve the calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Choose men who are loyal, trustworthy, discerning, and articulate to go and negotiate; something may yet be achieved that could ease our distress."

sentences.zh: 是時，百官議者，雖有異同，大概以和親為主焉。

translations.literal: At that time, among the officials who deliberated, though views differed, on the whole peace through marriage alliance was the main tendency.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the officials who deliberated differed in their views, but on the whole they favored seeking peace through alliance.

sentences.zh: 莊獻太子葬後，不置宮師官，升承旨為二品，以寵行簡，兼職如故。

translations.literal: After the burial of Crown Prince Zhuangxian the office of palace tutor was not re-established; the academician-in-ordinary was raised to second rank to honor Xingjian, his concurrent posts remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Zhuangxian was buried, the office of palace tutor was not re-established; the academician-in-ordinary was promoted to second rank as a mark of favor toward Xingjian, while his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，朝廷備防秋兵械，令內外職官不以丁憂致仕，皆納弓箭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year the court prepared autumn-defense weapons and ordered that civil and military officials, whether or not in mourning for a parent or retired, all submit bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year the court prepared weapons for the autumn defense and ordered that all officials within and outside the capital, whether mourning a parent or retired from office, must submit bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 行簡上書曰：「弓箭非通有之物，其清貧之家及中下監當，丁憂致仕，安有所謂如法軍器。

translations.literal: Xingjian memorialized: "Bows and arrows are not things universally possessed; in poor households and among middle and lower supervisory posts, those in mourning or retired—where would there be so-called regulation military gear?
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian memorialized, "Bows and arrows are not items every household possesses. Among the poor, those in middle and lower supervisory posts, and officials in mourning or retired from service—where would they obtain regulation military weapons?

sentences.zh: 今繩以軍期，補弊修壞，以求應命而已，與倉猝製造何以異哉。

translations.literal: Now binding them to military deadlines, patching the worn and repairing the broken merely to meet orders—how does this differ from hasty manufacture?
translations.idiomatic: Now they are bound to military deadlines and must patch together whatever is worn or broken merely to meet the order—how is this different from improvised manufacture in haste?

sentences.zh: 若於隨州郡及猛安謀克人戶拘括，擇其佳者買之，不足則令職輸所買之價，庶不擾而事可辦。」

translations.literal: If in the various prefectures and among meng'an and mouke households we register and select the better ones to purchase, and where insufficient require the official to pay the purchase price, perhaps without disturbance the matter may be accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: If in the various prefectures and among meng'an and mouke households we register households, select the better weapons for purchase, and where funds fall short require the official to pay the purchase price, the task might be accomplished without undue disturbance."

sentences.zh: 左丞相僕散端、平章政事高琪、盡忠、右丞賈益謙皆曰：「丁憂致仕者可以免此。」

translations.literal: The Left Chancellor Pusanduan, the Grand Councilors Gaoqi and Jinzong, and the Right Vice Minister Jia Yiqian all said: "Those in mourning or retired may be exempted from this."
translations.idiomatic: The left chancellor Pusanduan, the grand councilors Gaoqi and Jinzong, and the right vice minister Jia Yiqian all said, "Officials in mourning or retired should be exempted."

sentences.zh: 權參政烏古論德升曰：「職官久享爵祿，軍興以來，曾無寸補，況事已行而複改，天下何所取信。」

translations.literal: The Acting Grand Councilor Wugulun Desheng said: "Officials have long enjoyed titles and stipends; since military campaigns began they have not contributed the slightest aid—moreover, when a measure is already in force and then changed again, what faith can the realm place in us?"
translations.idiomatic: The acting grand councilor Wugulun Desheng said, "Officials have long enjoyed rank and stipends, yet since the wars began they have contributed nothing. Moreover, when a policy is already in force and then reversed, what faith can the realm place in the court?"

sentences.zh: 是議也，丁憂致仕官竟得免。

translations.literal: On this deliberation, officials in mourning or retired were in the end exempted.
translations.idiomatic: On this deliberation, officials in mourning or retired were ultimately exempted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，卒，贈銀青榮祿大夫，諡文正。

translations.literal: That year he died; he was posthumously granted Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master, with the posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died and was posthumously granted the title Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master, with the posthumous epithet Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 行簡端愨慎密，為人主所知。

translations.literal: Xingjian was upright, sincere, cautious, and discreet, and was understood by his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian was upright, sincere, cautious, and discreet, and won his sovereign's trust.

sentences.zh: 自初入翰林，至太常、禮部，典貢舉終身，縉紳以為榮。

translations.literal: From his first entry into the Hanlin through the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites, he oversaw the civil examinations throughout his life—the gentry regarded this as glory.
translations.idiomatic: From his first appointment to the Hanlin through his service at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites, he oversaw the civil examinations throughout his life—a distinction the gentry regarded as the highest honor.

sentences.zh: 與弟行信同居數十年，人無間言。

translations.literal: He lived together with his younger brother Xingxin for several decades, and no one spoke ill of them.
translations.idiomatic: He lived with his younger brother Xingxin for several decades without a word of reproach from anyone.

sentences.zh: 所著文章十五卷，《禮例纂》一百二十卷，會同、朝獻、禘佩、喪葬，皆有記錄，及《清台》，《皇華》、《戒嚴》、《為善》、《自公》等記，藏於家。

translations.literal: His writings comprised fifteen juan of essays, one hundred twenty juan of Collected Ritual Precedents, with records on joint audiences, court presentations, suburban and regalia rites, and funerals, as well as Clear Terrace, Imperial Splendor, Martial Alert, Doing Good, From the Duke, and other records, kept in his household.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included fifteen juan of essays and one hundred twenty juan of Collected Ritual Precedents, with records on joint audiences, court presentations, suburban and regalia rites, and funerals, as well as Clear Terrace, Imperial Splendor, Martial Alert, Doing Good, From the Duke, and other treatises, all kept in his household.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：張暐、行簡世為禮官，世習禮學。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Zhang Wei and Xingjian for generations were ritual officials and for generations studied ritual learning.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Zhang Wei and Xingjian were ritual officials for generations, and ritual learning ran in their family for generations.

sentences.zh: 其為禮也，行於家庭，講於朝廷，施用於鄰國，無不中度。

translations.literal: In their practice of ritual it was carried out in the family, expounded at court, and applied toward neighboring states—nothing failed to hit the measure.
translations.idiomatic: In their practice of ritual it was observed in the family, expounded at court, and applied in dealings with neighboring states—always to the proper measure.

sentences.zh: 古者官有世掌，學有專門，金諸儒臣，唯張氏父子庶幾無愧於古乎。

translations.literal: In antiquity offices had hereditary charge and learning had specialized schools; among the Jin scholar-officials, only the Zhang father and son perhaps nearly need not blush before antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity offices passed through families and learning had its specialists; among the Jin scholar-officials, only the Zhang father and son perhaps come nearest to matching the ancients without shame.

sentences.zh: 賈益謙

translations.literal: Jia Yiqian
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yiqian

sentences.zh: 賈益謙，字彥亨，沃州人也，本名守謙，避哀宗諱改焉。

translations.literal: Jia Yiqian, styled Yanheng, was a man of Wozhou; his original name was Shouqian, changed to avoid the taboo of Emperor Aizong.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yiqian, whose style name was Yanheng, came from Wozhou. His original name was Shouqian, which he changed to avoid the taboo name of Emperor Aizong.

sentences.zh: 大定十年詞賦進士，曆仕州郡，以能稱。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dading he passed the poetry-and-prose jinshi examination; he served through prefectures and commanderies and was known for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Dading era he passed the jinshi examination in poetry and prose, served in various prefectures and commanderies, and was known for his ability.

sentences.zh: 明昌間，入為尚書省令史，累遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: During the Mingchang era he entered as a clerk of the Department of State Affairs and was promoted in succession to Director of the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mingchang era he entered service as a clerk in the Department of State Affairs and rose in succession to director of the left bureau.

sentences.zh: 章宗諭之曰：「汝自知除至居是職，左司事不為不練，凡百官行止、資歷固宜照勘，勿使差繆。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangzong instructed him: "You yourself know from appointment to holding this post; affairs of the Left Bureau are not unpracticed—for all officials' movements and seniority you should certainly verify records and not allow errors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangzong told him, "You know yourself how you were appointed to this post. Affairs of the left bureau are not unfamiliar to you. You must verify every official's movements and seniority and allow no mistakes.

sentences.zh: 若武庫署直長移刺郝自平定州軍事判官召為典輿副轄，在職才五月，降授門山縣簿尉。

translations.literal: For example, Arms Repository Director Yila Hao was summoned from military adjutant of Pingding Prefecture to Deputy Commissioner of the Imperial Carriages; after only five months in office he was demoted to registrar and bailiff of Menshan County.
translations.idiomatic: For example, Yila Hao, director of the Arms Repository, was summoned from military adjutant at Pingding Prefecture to deputy commissioner of the Imperial Carriages, yet after only five months in office he was demoted to registrar and bailiff of Menshan County.

sentences.zh: 朕比閱貼黃，行止乃俱書作一十三月，行止尚如此失實，其如選法何？

translations.literal: I recently reviewed the yellow slips; his movements were both written as thirteen months—if movements are still so untrue, what of the selection law?
translations.idiomatic: I recently reviewed the personnel records, and his movements were both entered as thirteen months. If even movements are recorded so inaccurately, what becomes of the selection system?

sentences.zh: 蓋是汝不用心致然爾。

translations.literal: This is because you did not apply your mind and caused it.
translations.idiomatic: This happened because you did not apply yourself.

sentences.zh: 今姑杖知除掾，汝勿複犯之。」

translations.literal: For now I will merely cane the clerk who knew of the appointment; do not offend again."
translations.idiomatic: For now I will merely punish the appointment clerk; do not let this happen again."

sentences.zh: 五年，為右諫議大夫，上言：「提刑司官不須遣監察體訪，宜據其任內行事，考其能否而升黜之。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year he became Right Remonstrator and memorialized: "Investigation commissioners need not send surveillance officers to inquire in person; they should judge by actions within their term of office, examine ability, and promote or demote accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became right remonstrator and memorialized, "Investigation commissioners need not send surveillance officers to conduct field inquiries. They should judge officials by their conduct during their terms of office, assess their competence, and promote or demote them accordingly."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿之言其有所見乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Does your statement rest on some observation?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Does your view rest on some particular observation?"

sentences.zh: 守謙對曰：「提刑官若不稱職，眾所共知，且其職與監察等，臣是故言之。」

translations.literal: Shouqian replied: "If an investigation commissioner is unfit for his post, all know it together; moreover his duties equal those of surveillance officers—your subject therefore spoke."
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian answered, "If an investigation commissioner is unfit for his post, everyone knows it. Moreover, his duties are equivalent to those of a surveillance officer—that is why I spoke as I did."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，上將幸景明宮清暑，守謙連上疏，極諫之。

translations.literal: That summer the emperor was about to visit Jingming Palace for summer coolness; Shouqian submitted successive memorials remonstrating to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when the emperor planned to visit Jingming Palace to escape the heat, Shouqian submitted successive memorials remonstrating against the journey in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 上禦後閣，召守謙入對，稱旨。

translations.literal: The emperor attended the rear pavilion, summoned Shouqian to answer, and his words accorded with the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him in the rear pavilion, summoned Shouqian to answer in person, and was pleased with his responses.

sentences.zh: 進兼尚書吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to concurrent Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to serve concurrently as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時鎬王以疑忌下獄，上怒甚，朝臣無敢言者。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Hao was imprisoned on suspicion; the emperor's anger was extreme, and no court official dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Hao was imprisoned on suspicion, and the emperor's anger was so fierce that no court official dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 守謙上章論其不可，言極懇切。

translations.literal: Shouqian submitted a memorial arguing that this could not be done, his words extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian submitted a memorial arguing that this must not be done, speaking with utmost earnestness.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「汝言諸王皆有覬心，而遊其門者不無橫議。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "You say all the princes harbor covetous hearts, and those who frequent their gates do not lack reckless talk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "You say all the princes harbor ambitions, and those who frequent their gates do not lack reckless talk.

sentences.zh: 此何等語，固當罪汝。

translations.literal: What sort of language is this? You should indeed be punished.
translations.idiomatic: What sort of language is this? You certainly deserve punishment.

sentences.zh: 以汝前言事亦有當處，故免。」

translations.literal: Because in your earlier words there were also points that fit, you are therefore spared."
translations.idiomatic: Because your earlier remonstrances also had merit, I spare you."

sentences.zh: 既而以議鎬王事有違上意，解職，削官二階。

translations.literal: Thereafter, because his discussion of the Prince of Hao affair went against the emperor's intent, he was removed from office and his rank was reduced by two steps.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, because his counsel on the Prince of Hao went against the emperor's wishes, he was dismissed from office and his rank was reduced by two steps.

sentences.zh: 承安元年七月，降為甯化州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Cheng'an he was demoted to Prefect of Ninghua.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of the Cheng'an era he was demoted to prefect of Ninghua.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，改為山東路按察使，轉河北西路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year he was changed to Investigation Commissioner of Shandong Circuit and transferred to Transport Commissioner of Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year he was reassigned as investigation commissioner of Shandong Circuit, then transferred to transport commissioner of Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年四月，召為禦史中丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Taihe he was summoned as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of the Taihe era he was recalled to serve as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，出為定武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year he went out as Military Commissioner of Dingwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year he was sent out to serve as military commissioner of the Dingwu Army.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，複為禦史中丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year he again became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year he again became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 八月，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was changed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔守謙等一十三員分詣諸路，與本路按察司官一員同推排民戶物力。

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict ordered Shouqian and twelve others to go separately to the various circuits, each together with one investigation official of that circuit to reassess household property ratings.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict ordered Shouqian and twelve others to travel to the various circuits, each together with one local investigation official, to reassess household property ratings.

sentences.zh: 上召見於香閣，諭之曰：「朕選卿等隨路推排，除推收外，其新強、銷乏戶，雖集眾推唱，然銷乏者勿銷不盡，如一戶元物力三百貫，今蠲減二百五十貫，猶有不能當。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned them at the Fragrant Pavilion and instructed: "I have chosen you to reassess along each circuit; apart from increases and reductions, for newly prosperous and declining households—though the crowd may jointly propose—yet for declining households do not reduce to nothing; if one household originally rated three hundred strings of property and now is exempted two hundred fifty, there may still be cases that cannot bear even that.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received them in the Fragrant Pavilion and instructed, "I have chosen you to conduct reassessments along each circuit. Beyond standard increases and reductions, for newly prosperous and declining households—though the community may jointly propose figures—for declining households do not reduce the assessment to nothing. If a household originally rated at three hundred strings is now reduced by two hundred fifty, some may still be unable to bear even the remainder.

sentences.zh: 新強者勿添盡，量存氣力，如一戶添三百貫而止添二百貫之類。

translations.literal: For newly prosperous households do not add to the full limit; measure and leave them strength—as when one household could bear three hundred strings added but you add only two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: For newly prosperous households do not raise assessments to the full limit; leave them some capacity to pay—as when a household could bear an increase of three hundred strings but you raise it by only two hundred.

sentences.zh: 卿等宜各用心。

translations.literal: You should each apply your minds.
translations.idiomatic: Each of you must apply yourselves conscientiously.

sentences.zh: 百姓應當賦役，十年之間，利害非細。

translations.literal: The people's obligations of tax and corvée over ten years—the benefit and harm are not slight.
translations.idiomatic: The people's tax and corvée obligations over the next ten years will turn on this; the consequences are no small matter.

sentences.zh: 苟不稱所委，治罪當不輕也。」

translations.literal: If you do not match what is entrusted, punishment should not be light."
translations.idiomatic: If you fail to meet what is entrusted to you, the penalties will not be light."

sentences.zh: 尋出知濟南府，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: Soon after he went out as prefect of Jinan and was transferred to garrison at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was sent out as prefect of Jinan, then transferred to the garrison at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 大安末，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: At the end of Da'an he was appointed Participant in Government.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Da'an era he was appointed participant in government.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年二月，改河東南路安撫使，俄知彰德府。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhenyou he was changed to Pacification Commissioner of Hedong South Circuit; soon after he became prefect of Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of the Zhenyou era he was made pacification commissioner of Hedong South Circuit, and soon afterward became prefect of Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 三年，召為尚書省右丞。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled to serve as right vice minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會宣宗始遷汴梁，益謙乃建言：「汴之形勢，惟恃大河。

translations.literal: As Emperor Xuanzong was first moving the capital to Bianliang, Yiqian then proposed: "Bian's strategic position relies solely on the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Emperor Xuanzong was moving the capital to Bianliang, Yiqian proposed, "Bian's strategic position depends entirely on the Great River.

sentences.zh: 今河朔受兵，群盜並起，宜嚴河禁以備不虞，凡自北來而無公憑者，勿聽渡。」

translations.literal: Now Hebei north of the river suffers warfare and bandits rise together; river crossings should be strictly forbidden to guard against the unexpected—all coming from the north without official credentials must not be allowed to cross."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Hebei region north of the river is under attack and bandits are rising everywhere. River crossings should be strictly controlled as a precaution: anyone coming from the north without official credentials must not be allowed to cross."

sentences.zh: 是時，河北民遷避河南者甚眾。

translations.literal: At that time many people of Hebei migrated to escape south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a great many people from Hebei fled south across the river to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 侍御史劉無規上言：「僑戶宜與土民均應差役。」

translations.literal: Attending Censor Liu Wugui memorialized: "Migrant households should share corvée duties equally with native residents."
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Liu Wugui memorialized, "Migrant households should bear corvée duties on the same terms as local residents."

sentences.zh: 上留中，而自以其意問宰臣。

translations.literal: The emperor kept it within the palace and himself asked the chief ministers his own intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withheld the memorial and privately asked the chief ministers for their views.

sentences.zh: 丞相端、平章盡忠以為便。

translations.literal: Chancellor Duan and Grand Councilor Jinzong thought it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Duan and Grand Councilor Jinzong thought the proposal expedient.

sentences.zh: 益謙曰：「僑戶應役，甚非計也。

translations.literal: Yiqian said: "Having migrant households bear corvée is a very poor plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqian said, "Requiring migrant households to bear corvée would be a grave mistake.

sentences.zh: 蓋河北人戶本避兵而來，兵稍息即歸矣。

translations.literal: For Hebei households originally came to escape warfare; when warfare eases slightly they will return.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Hebei came here to escape the fighting; when the warfare subsides even slightly, they will return home.

sentences.zh: 今旅寓倉皇之際，無以為生，若又與地著者並應供憶，必騷動不能安居矣。

translations.literal: Now in the haste of lodging as travelers they have no means to live; if they must also share obligations with settled natives, they will surely be disturbed and unable to settle in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in their haste as refugees, they barely have the means to live. If they must also share obligations with local residents, they will surely be driven to unrest and unable to settle in peace.

sentences.zh: 豈主上矜恤流亡之意乎。」

translations.literal: Is this the sovereign's intent to pity and comfort the exiled?"
translations.idiomatic: Would that accord with Your Majesty's intent to show compassion to those in exile?"

sentences.zh: 上甚嘉賞，曰：「此非朕意也。」

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised and rewarded him, saying: "This was not my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly praised him and said, "That was never my intent."

sentences.zh: 因出元規章示之。

translations.literal: He then produced Wugui's memorial and showed it.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced Wugui's memorial and showed it to them.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，進拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year he was advanced and appointed Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year he was promoted to left vice minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，致仕，居鄭州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he retired from office and dwelt at Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he retired from office and lived at Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：賈益謙于衛紹王，可謂盡事君之義矣。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Jia Yiqian toward Prince Shao of Wei may be said to have fulfilled the duty of serving one's lord.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: In his service to Prince Shao of Wei, Jia Yiqian may be said to have fulfilled every obligation of loyalty to his lord.

sentences.zh: 海陵之事，君子不無憾焉。

translations.literal: In the affair of Emperor Hailing, gentlemen do not lack regret.
translations.idiomatic: In the affair of Emperor Hailing, men of principle cannot but feel regret.

sentences.zh: 夫正隆之為惡，暴其大者斯亦足矣。

translations.literal: As for the evils of the Zhenglong era, exposing the greatest of them is already sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: As for the crimes of the Zhenglong era, exposing the greatest of them is already sufficient.

sentences.zh: 中綍之醜，史不絕書，誠如益謙所言，則史亦可為取富貴之道乎？

translations.literal: The filth of the inner court—history does not cease recording it; if it were truly as Yiqian said, could history also become a path to gaining wealth and honor?
translations.idiomatic: The scandals of the inner court fill the historical record without end. If it were truly as Yiqian said, could history itself become merely a path to wealth and rank?

sentences.zh: 嘻，其甚矣。

translations.literal: Alas, how excessive!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how far it had gone!

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「不有廢者，其何以興！」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "If there were none discarded, how could there be rising!"
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, "If there were none cast aside, how could any rise?"

sentences.zh: 劉炳，葛城人。

translations.literal: Liu Bing was a man of Gecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing came from Gecheng.

sentences.zh: 每讀書，見前古忠臣烈士為國家畫策慮萬世安，輒歎息景慕。

translations.literal: Whenever he read books and saw ancient loyal ministers and martyrs who devised plans for the state and considered the security of ten thousand generations, he would sigh and admire them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read of loyal ministers and martyrs of old who devised strategies for the state and planned for the security of generations to come, he would sigh with admiration.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，中進士第，即日上書條便宜十事：

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou he passed the jinshi examination; that same day he memorialized setting forth ten measures of expedient policy:
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhenyou era he passed the jinshi examination and that same day memorialized setting forth ten measures of urgent policy:

sentences.zh: 其一曰，任諸王以鎮社稷。

translations.literal: The first said: Entrust the princes to secure the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The first proposed entrusting the imperial princes to secure the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 臣觀往歲，王師屢戰屢衄，率皆自敗。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that in past years the royal army fought repeatedly and was repeatedly defeated—mostly through self-defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes that in recent years the imperial armies have fought repeatedly and been repeatedly defeated—mostly through their own failures.

sentences.zh: 承平日久，人不知兵，將帥非才，既無靖難之謀，又無效死之節，外托持重之名，而內為自安之計，擇驍果以自隨，委疲懦以臨陣，陣勢稍動，望塵先奔，士卒從而大潰。

translations.literal: Long peace had made men ignorant of war; commanders lacked talent, having neither plans to quell calamity nor resolve to die in effect. Outwardly they bore the name of steadiness, inwardly they plotted self-preservation—choosing fierce fighters to follow themselves and assigning the weary and weak to face battle. When the formation stirred slightly they fled at the sight of dust, and the soldiers followed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace the people had forgotten war, and the commanders lacked ability. They had neither plans to quell the crisis nor the resolve to die in battle. Outwardly they affected gravity; inwardly they schemed for their own safety—keeping the brave at their side while sending the weak and timid to face the enemy. At the slightest stir in the ranks they fled at the first sight of dust, and the soldiers followed in total rout.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不加詰問，輒為益兵。

translations.literal: The court did not interrogate them but merely added more troops for them.
translations.idiomatic: The court never held them accountable but merely reinforced their armies.

sentences.zh: 是以法度日紊，倉庾日虛，閭井日凋，土地日蹙。

translations.literal: Thus law and institutions daily fell into disorder, granaries daily emptied, villages daily withered, and territory daily shrank.
translations.idiomatic: Thus law and order fell daily into disorder, the granaries emptied, villages withered, and territory shrank.

sentences.zh: 自大駕南巡，遠近相望，益無固志。

translations.literal: Since the imperial carriage toured south, near and far looked to one another, and resolve grew ever less firm.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor's tour to the south, people near and far have looked to one another in uncertainty, and their resolve has grown ever weaker.

sentences.zh: 吏任河北者以為不幸，逡巡退避，莫之敢前。

translations.literal: Officials appointed to Hebei regarded it as misfortune, hesitated and shrank back, and none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: Officials appointed to Hebei regarded their posts as a misfortune, hesitated and shrank back, and none dared press forward.

sentences.zh: 昔唐天寶之末，洛陽、潼關相次失守，皇輿夜出，向非太子回趨靈武，率先諸將，則西行之士當終老於劍南矣。

translations.literal: Formerly at the end of Tang Tianbao, Luoyang and Tong Pass fell in succession; the imperial carriage fled by night. Had the crown prince not turned back toward Lingwu and taken the lead before the generals, those who went west would have ended their lives in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tang Tianbao era, Luoyang and Tong Pass fell in succession and the emperor fled by night. Had the crown prince not turned back toward Lingwu and taken the lead before the generals, those who fled west would have ended their days in exile in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下擇諸王之英明者，總監天下之兵，北駐重鎮，移檄遠近，戒以軍政。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that Your Majesty select the enlightened among the princes to oversee all armies under Heaven, garrison the north at a strategic stronghold, send proclamations near and far, and warn them with military discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that Your Majesty select the most capable among the imperial princes to command all armies under Heaven, station them in the north at a strategic stronghold, send proclamations throughout the realm, and enforce strict military discipline.

sentences.zh: 則四方聞風者皆將自奮，前死不避。

translations.literal: Then all who hear the wind in the four quarters will rouse themselves and not shrink from death in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Then all who hear of it throughout the realm will rouse themselves and face death without flinching.

sentences.zh: 折沖厭難，無大於此。

translations.literal: To repel enemies and overcome hardship—nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: There is no greater means of repelling the enemy and overcoming hardship than this.

sentences.zh: 夫人情可以氣激不可以力使，一卒先登，則萬夫齊奮，此古人所以先身教而後威令也。

translations.literal: Human sentiment may be roused by spirit but cannot be driven by force; when one soldier mounts first, then ten thousand men rise together—this is why the ancients first taught by personal example and afterward enforced commands.
translations.idiomatic: Human hearts may be stirred by spirit but cannot be driven by force alone. When one soldier climbs the wall first, ten thousand follow in ardor—that is why the ancients led by personal example before enforcing commands.

sentences.zh: 二曰，結人心以固基本。

translations.literal: The second said: Bind men's hearts to secure the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The second proposed binding the people's hearts to secure the foundation of the state.

sentences.zh: 天子惠人，不在施予，在於除其同患，因所利而利之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's favoring the people lies not in bestowing gifts but in removing their shared afflictions and benefiting them through what they already find profitable.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven benefits the people not through gifts but by removing their shared afflictions and advancing their interests through what they already find advantageous.

sentences.zh: 今艱危之後，易於為惠，因其欲安而慰撫之，則忠誠親上之心，當益加於前日。

translations.literal: Now after hardship and peril it is easy to show favor; following their desire for peace, comfort and reassure them—then the heart of loyalty and closeness to superiors should increase beyond the day before.
translations.idiomatic: Now, after hardship and peril, it is easier than ever to show true favor. Respond to their longing for peace with comfort and reassurance, and their loyalty and devotion to the throne will grow stronger than before.

sentences.zh: 臣願寬其賦役，信其號令，凡事不便者一切停罷。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to lighten their taxes and corvée, trust their commands, and stop and abolish everything that is inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that their taxes and labor levies be eased, that they be allowed to trust your commands, and that every burdensome measure be halted altogether.

sentences.zh: 時遣重臣按行郡縣，延見耆老，問其疾苦，選廉正，黜貪殘，拯貧窮，恤孤獨，勞來還定，則效忠徇義，無有二志矣。

translations.literal: From time to time send weighty ministers to inspect commanderies and counties, extend audience to elders, ask their hardships, select the upright and incorrupt, dismiss the greedy and cruel, rescue the poor, pity the orphaned and alone, comfort those who come and settle those who return—then they will devote loyalty and follow righteousness, and will have no second intent.
translations.idiomatic: Send senior ministers from time to time to tour the commanderies and counties, summon the elders, inquire into their hardships, promote the upright, dismiss the greedy and cruel, relieve the poor, care for orphans and the destitute, and comfort those who come and settle those who return. Then they will serve with loyalty and righteousness and harbor no second thoughts.

sentences.zh: 故曰安民可與行義，危民易與為亂，惟陛下留神。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: with the people secure one may practice righteousness with them; with the people in peril it is easy to make them rebel—may Your Majesty give this thought.
