translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: when the people are secure, they may be led in righteous deeds; when they are in peril, they are easily driven to rebellion. May Your Majesty give this your close attention.

sentences.zh: 三曰，廣收人材以備國用。

translations.literal: The third said: Broadly gather talent to prepare the state's needs.
translations.idiomatic: The third proposed broadly recruiting talent to meet the needs of the state.

sentences.zh: 備歲寒者必求貂狐，適長途者必畜騏驥。

translations.literal: One who prepares for the year's cold must seek sable and fox fur; one who fits himself for a long road must keep excellent steeds.
translations.idiomatic: He who prepares for winter's cold must seek sable and fox fur; he who readies himself for a long journey must keep swift horses.

sentences.zh: 河南、陝西，車駕臨幸，當有以大慰士民之心。

translations.literal: In Henan and Shaanxi, where the imperial carriage has sojourned, there ought to be means greatly to comfort the hearts of gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan and Shaanxi, where the imperial carriage has toured, there should be measures to greatly reassure the hearts of scholars and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 其有操行為民望者，稍擢用之，平居可以勵風俗，緩急可以備驅策。

translations.literal: Among those whose conduct makes them the people's hope, promote and employ them somewhat; in ordinary times they may encourage custom, in urgency they may be kept for driving and deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Among those whose conduct commands public respect, promote them gradually. In peaceful times they may uplift local morals; in emergencies they may be called upon for service.

sentences.zh: 昭示新恩，易民觀聽，陰系天下之心也。

translations.literal: To display new favor, change what the people see and hear, and secretly bind the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This would proclaim fresh grace, transform what the people see and hear, and quietly win the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 四曰，選守令以安百姓。

translations.literal: The fourth said: Select prefects and magistrates to settle the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth proposed selecting capable prefects and magistrates to secure the welfare of the people.

sentences.zh: 郡守、縣令，天子所恃以為治，百姓所依以為命者也。

translations.literal: Prefects and county magistrates are those on whom the Son of Heaven relies for governance and on whom the hundred surnames rely for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and county magistrates are those on whom the Son of Heaven relies to govern and on whom the people rely for their very livelihood.

sentences.zh: 今眾庶已弊，官吏庸暗，無安利之才，貪暴昏亂，與奸為市，公有鬥粟之賦，私有萬錢之求，遠近囂囂，無所控告。

translations.literal: Now the multitude is already exhausted; officials are mediocre and dim, without talent to bring benefit and peace, greedy and violent, muddled and chaotic, trafficking with the wicked. Publicly there is tax of a peck of grain; privately demands of ten thousand cash. Near and far clamor with no place to lodge complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The people are already exhausted, while officials are mediocre and corrupt, lacking any talent to bring benefit or order. They are greedy, violent, and chaotic, colluding with criminals. Official levies take a peck of grain while private demands reach ten thousand cash. Complaints rise everywhere, yet there is nowhere to seek redress.

sentences.zh: 自今非才器過人，政跡卓異者，不可使在此職。

translations.literal: From now on, unless talent and capacity surpass others and administrative traces are outstanding, one must not be placed in these offices.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth none but those of exceptional talent and distinguished administrative record should hold these offices.

sentences.zh: 親勳故舊，雖望隆資高，不可使為長吏。

translations.literal: Kin, meritorious fellows, and old associates—though their repute be lofty and seniority high—must not be made chief local administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Kin, meritorious associates, and old companions—however eminent their standing—must not be appointed as chief local administrators.

sentences.zh: 則賢者喜於殊用，益盡其能，不肖者愧慕而思自勵矣。

translations.literal: Then the worthy will rejoice at special employment and further exhaust their ability; the unworthy will feel shame and admiration and think to encourage themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Then the worthy will rejoice at exceptional appointment and give their utmost; the unworthy will feel shame and emulation and strive to improve themselves.

sentences.zh: 五曰，褒忠義以勵臣節。

translations.literal: The fifth said: Commend loyalty and righteousness to encourage ministers' integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth proposed honoring loyalty and righteousness to inspire integrity among officials.

sentences.zh: 忠義之士，奮身效命，力盡城破而不少屈。

translations.literal: Men of loyalty and righteousness throw themselves forward to give their lives, exhausting their strength until the city fell yet not bending in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Men of loyalty and righteousness threw themselves into battle and gave their lives, fighting until strength was spent and the city had fallen, yet never yielding.

sentences.zh: 事定之後，有司略不加省，棄職者顧以恩貸，死事者反不見錄，天下何所慕憚，而不為自安之計邪？

translations.literal: After affairs were settled, the responsible offices barely gave them consideration; those who abandoned their posts were instead shown grace, while those who died in service were not recorded—what in all under Heaven is there to admire and fear, that they would not make plans for their own security?
translations.idiomatic: After the crisis passed, the responsible offices scarcely acknowledged them. Those who had abandoned their posts were shown leniency, while those who died in service went unrewarded. What is there left in the realm to admire or fear, that officials would not simply look to their own safety?

sentences.zh: 使為臣者皆知殺身之無益，臨難可以苟免，甚非國家之利也。

translations.literal: To make ministers all know that giving their lives is without benefit, and that facing hardship they may escape as they can—this is greatly not the state's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers learn that sacrificing their lives brings no reward and that in crisis they may save themselves by any means, this can only harm the state.

sentences.zh: 六曰，務農力本以廣蓄積。

translations.literal: The sixth said: Devote effort to agriculture and strengthen the foundation to broaden stored accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth proposed devoting effort to agriculture and strengthening the economic foundation to build up reserves.

sentences.zh: 此最強兵富民之要術，當今之急務也。

translations.literal: This is the essential art for strengthening armies and enriching the people, and the urgent task of the present day.
translations.idiomatic: This is the essential means of strengthening the army and enriching the people, and the most urgent task of the day.

sentences.zh: 七曰，崇節儉以省財用。

translations.literal: The seventh said: Uphold frugality to economize expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh proposed promoting frugality to reduce state expenditure.

sentences.zh: 今海內虛耗，田疇荒蕪，廢奢從儉以紓生民之急，無先於此者。

translations.literal: Now within the seas resources are depleted and fields lie waste and overgrown; to abandon extravagance and follow frugality to ease the people's urgent distress—nothing comes before this.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is depleted and fields lie fallow. To abandon extravagance and embrace frugality in order to relieve the people's distress—nothing should take precedence over this.

sentences.zh: 八曰，去冗食以助軍費。

translations.literal: The eighth said: Remove redundant consumption to assist military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth proposed eliminating redundant offices and salaries to support military expenditure.

sentences.zh: 兵革之後，人物凋喪者十四五，郡縣官吏署置如故，甚非審權救弊之道。

translations.literal: After arms and armor, four or five in ten of the people had withered and perished, yet commandery and county officials and offices were established as before—this is greatly not the way of weighing power and saving from ruin.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars, four or five in ten of the population had perished, yet commandery and county offices remained as numerous as before. This is hardly the way to weigh circumstances and remedy disaster.

sentences.zh: 九曰，修軍政以習守戰。

translations.literal: The ninth said: Repair military administration to practice defense and battle.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth proposed restoring military discipline to train troops in defense and combat.

sentences.zh: 自古名將料敵制勝，訓練士卒，故可使赴湯蹈火，百戰不殆。

translations.literal: Since antiquity famous generals have gauged the enemy and controlled victory, trained soldiers and troops—thus they could be made to brave boiling water and tread fire, and in a hundred battles not be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, famous generals have assessed the enemy to secure victory and trained their troops so thoroughly that men would brave fire and water and emerge unscathed from a hundred battles.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「以不教民戰，是謂棄之。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "To use the people in battle without teaching them—this is called abandoning them."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "To send the people into battle without training them is to abandon them."

sentences.zh: 兵法曰：「器械不利，以其卒與敵也。

translations.literal: The Art of War says: "If weapons and equipment are not sharp, it is as though one gave one's soldiers to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War says, "If weapons are inadequate, it is as though one hands one's troops to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 卒不服習，以其將與敵也。

translations.literal: If soldiers are not trained and practiced, it is as though one gave one's general to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If soldiers are ill-trained, it is as though one hands one's general to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 將不知兵，以其主與敵也。

translations.literal: If the general does not understand warfare, it is as though one gave one's lord to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If the general does not understand warfare, it is as though one hands one's sovereign to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 主不擇將，以其國與敵也。」

translations.literal: If the lord does not select his generals, it is as though one gave one's state to the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign does not choose his generals wisely, it is as though one hands one's state to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 可不慎哉。

translations.literal: Can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Can one not take heed!

sentences.zh: 十曰，修城池以備守禦。

translations.literal: The tenth said: Repair city walls and moats to prepare defense.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth proposed repairing city walls and fortifications to prepare for defense.

sentences.zh: 保障國家，惟都城與附近數郡耳。

translations.literal: To secure and protect the state depends only on the capital and the several nearby commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The security of the state depends only on the capital and the surrounding commanderies.

sentences.zh: 北地不守，是無河朔矣，黃河豈足恃哉。

translations.literal: If the northern lands are not held, then there is no Hebei; how can the Yellow River alone be relied upon!
translations.idiomatic: If the northern territories are not held, Hebei is lost. How can the Yellow River alone be trusted as a defense?

sentences.zh: 書奏，宣宗異焉。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Xuanzong was struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Xuanzong was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 復試之曰：「河北城邑，何術可保？

translations.literal: He again tested him, saying: "The cities and towns of Hebei—by what method can they be secured?
translations.idiomatic: He summoned him again for questioning and said, "The cities and towns of Hebei—by what means can they be secured?

sentences.zh: 兵民雜居，何道可和？

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians dwell mixed together—by what way can they be harmonized?
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians live intermingled—by what means can they live in harmony?

sentences.zh: 鈔法如何而通？

translations.literal: How may paper currency policy be made to circulate?
translations.idiomatic: How can paper currency be made to circulate effectively?

sentences.zh: 物價如何而平？」

translations.literal: How may commodity prices be leveled?"
translations.idiomatic: How can commodity prices be stabilized?"

sentences.zh: 炳對大略以審擇守將則城邑固，兵不侵民則兵民和，斂散相權則鈔法通，勸農薄賦則物價平。

translations.literal: Bing replied in broad outline: if defending generals are carefully chosen then cities and towns are secure; if soldiers do not encroach on civilians then soldiers and civilians are harmonious; if collection and distribution are mutually weighed then paper currency circulates; if agriculture is encouraged and levies lightened then commodity prices are level.
translations.idiomatic: Bing answered in outline: carefully select defending generals and the cities will hold firm; keep soldiers from harassing civilians and army and people will live in harmony; balance collection and disbursement and paper currency will circulate; encourage farming and lighten taxes and prices will stabilize.

sentences.zh: 宣宗雖異其言，而不能用，但補禦史台令史而已。

translations.literal: Although Emperor Xuanzong was struck by his words, he could not employ him, but only supplemented him as a clerk in the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor was impressed by his answers, he did not put them into practice and merely appointed Bing a clerk in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 論曰：劉炳可謂能言之士矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Liu Bing may be called a man able to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Liu Bing may truly be called a man of eloquent counsel.

sentences.zh: 宣宗召試既不失對，而以一台令史賞之，足以倡士氣乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong summoned and tested him, and he did not fail in reply—yet rewarded him with only a single Censorate clerkship; is that enough to lead scholars' morale?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong summoned him for examination and he answered without fault, yet rewarded him with no more than a clerkship in the Censorate. Was that enough to inspire the morale of scholars?

sentences.zh: 朮虎高琪

translations.literal: Paihu Gaoqi
translations.idiomatic: Paihu Gaoqi

sentences.zh: 朮虎高琪，或作高乞，西北路猛安人。

translations.literal: Paihu Gaoqi—also written Gaoqi—was a man of the Meng'an of the Northwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Paihu Gaoqi, also written Gaoqi, came from the Meng'an of the Northwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定二十七年充護衛，轉十人長，出職河間都總管判官，召為武衛軍鈐轄，遷宿直將軍，除建州刺史，改同知監洮府事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Dading he filled the Imperial Guard, was transferred to leader of ten, left office as adjunct judge of the Hejian Metropolitan Commandant, was summoned as Controller of the Martial Guard Army, was promoted to Garrison Duty General, appointed Prefect of Jianzhou, and changed to Associate Commissioner of the Tao Prefecture Superintendency.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of the Dading reign he joined the Imperial Guard, rose to leader of ten, served as adjunct judge under the Hejian metropolitan commandant, was summoned as controller of the Martial Guard Army, promoted to garrison duty general, appointed prefect of Jianzhou, and then made associate commissioner of the Tao Prefecture superintendency.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，伐宋，與彰化軍節度副使把回海備鞏州諸鎮，宋兵萬余自鞏州轆轤嶺入，高琪奮擊破之，賜銀百兩、重彩十端。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, campaigning against Song, together with Vice Commissioner of the Zhanghua Army Ba Huihai he prepared the garrisons of Gong Prefecture; more than ten thousand Song troops entered from the Luolu Ridge of Gong Prefecture. Gaoqi struck fiercely and defeated them, and was granted one hundred taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Taihe era, during the campaign against Song, he joined Vice Commissioner Ba Huihai of the Zhanghua Army in defending the garrisons of Gong Prefecture. When more than ten thousand Song troops entered through Luolu Ridge, Gaoqi attacked fiercely and routed them. He was rewarded with one hundred taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy brocade.

sentences.zh: 青宜可內附，詔知府事石抹仲溫與高琪俱出界，與青宜可合兵進取。

translations.literal: When Qing Yi Ke submitted inward, an edict ordered Prefectural Commissioner Shimo Zhongwen and Gaoqi together to go beyond the border and join forces with Qing Yi Ke to advance and seize.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing Yi Ke submitted to Jin allegiance, an edict ordered Prefectural Commissioner Shimo Zhongwen and Gaoqi to cross the border together and join Qing Yi Ke in a joint advance.

sentences.zh: 詔高琪曰：「汝年尚少，近聞與宋人力戰奮勇，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: An edict told Gaoqi: "You are still young; recently I have heard that in fierce battle with the Song you were valiant—I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict addressed Gaoqi: "You are still young, yet I have heard that in fierce combat with the Song you fought with great valor. I am deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 今與仲溫同行出界，如其成功，高爵厚祿，朕不吝也。」

translations.literal: Now go beyond the border together with Zhongwen; if you succeed, high rank and thick salary—I shall not be sparing."
translations.idiomatic: Go beyond the border now with Zhongwen. If you succeed, high rank and generous rewards shall be yours—I shall not be sparing."

sentences.zh: 詔封吳曦為蜀國王，高琪為封冊使。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Wu Xi as King of Shu; Gaoqi was made enfeoffment envoy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed Wu Xi as King of Shu and appointed Gaoqi envoy of investiture.

sentences.zh: 詔戒諭曰：「卿讀書解事，蜀人亦識威名，勿以財賄動心，失大國體。

translations.literal: An edict admonished him: "You read books and understand affairs; the people of Shu also know your martial renown—do not let wealth and bribes move your heart and lose the great state's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: The edict cautioned him: "You are educated and understand affairs, and the people of Shu know your reputation. Do not let gifts and bribes sway you and compromise the dignity of the great state.

sentences.zh: 如或隨去奉職有違禮生事，卿與喬宇體察以聞。」

translations.literal: If any who follow and go to serve there violate ritual and stir up trouble, you and Qiao Yu are to investigate and report."
translations.idiomatic: If any member of the entourage violates protocol or causes trouble, you and Qiao Yu are to investigate and report."

sentences.zh: 使還，加都統，號平南虎威將軍。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, he was advanced to commander-in-chief and styled General Who Pacifies the South with Tiger Might.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return, he was promoted to commander-in-chief and given the title General Who Pacifies the South with Tiger Might.

sentences.zh: 宋安丙遣李孝義率步騎三萬攻秦州，先以萬人圍皁角堡，高琪赴之。

translations.literal: Song Anbing sent Li Xiaoyi leading thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Qin Prefecture; first with ten thousand men he besieged Zaojiao Fort, and Gaoqi went to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Song Anbing sent Li Xiaoyi at the head of thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Qin Prefecture. Li first invested Zaojiao Fort with ten thousand men, and Gaoqi marched to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 宋兵列陣山谷，以武車為左右翼，伏弩其下來逆戰。

translations.literal: Song troops arrayed battle lines in valleys and ravines, with war chariots as left and right wings; crossbows were hidden beneath to come out and meet battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Song forces drew up in the valleys with war chariots forming the wings and crossbowmen concealed below, ready to meet the attack.

sentences.zh: 既合，宋兵陽卻。

translations.literal: Once they joined battle, the Song troops feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Once battle was joined, the Song troops feigned retreat.

sentences.zh: 高琪軍見宋兵伏不得前，退整陣，宋兵複來。

translations.literal: Gaoqi's army, seeing Song ambush and unable to advance, withdrew and reformed the array; the Song troops came again.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the ambush, Gaoqi's troops could not advance and withdrew to reform their ranks, whereupon the Song forces pressed forward again.

sentences.zh: 凡五戰，宋兵益堅，不可以得志。

translations.literal: In all five engagements the Song troops grew ever firmer, and he could not achieve his intent.
translations.idiomatic: After five engagements the Song line held ever firmer, and he could not gain the upper hand.

sentences.zh: 高琪分騎為二，出者戰則止者俟，止者出則戰者還，還者複出以更。

translations.literal: Gaoqi divided his cavalry in two: those who went out fought while those who halted waited; when those who halted went out, those who fought returned, and those who returned went out again in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi divided his cavalry in two. One wing fought while the other waited; when the waiting wing charged, the fighting wing withdrew, then returned to the fray in rotation.

sentences.zh: 久之，遣蒲察桃思剌潛兵上山，自山馳下合擊，大破宋兵，斬首四千級，生擒數百人，李孝義乃解圍去。

translations.literal: After a long while he sent Pucha Taosila with troops secretly up the mountain; from the mountain they galloped down in combined strike, greatly defeating Song troops—four thousand heads cut, several hundred captured alive—and Li Xiaoyi then lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he sent Pucha Taosila with troops up the mountain by a hidden route. They charged down the slopes in a combined assault and routed the Song army, taking four thousand heads and capturing several hundred alive. Li Xiaoyi then lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宋兵三千致馬連寨以窺湫池，遣夾谷福壽擊走之，斬七百餘級。

translations.literal: Three thousand Song troops reached Malian Stockade to spy on Qiu Pool; he sent Jiagu Fushou to strike and drive them off, cutting more than seven hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: When three thousand Song troops advanced to Malian Stockade to threaten Qiu Pool, he sent Jiagu Fushou to drive them off, taking more than seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，累官泰州刺史，以颭軍三千屯通玄門外。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an, through successive offices he became Prefect of Taizhou and garrisoned three thousand campaign troops outside Tongxuan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Da'an era he rose through successive posts to prefect of Taizhou and garrisoned three thousand campaign troops outside Tongxuan Gate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，升縉山縣為鎮州，以高琪為防禦使，權元帥右都監，所部颭軍賞賚有差。

translations.literal: Before long Jinshan County was elevated to Zhen Prefecture; Gaoqi was made defense commissioner, acting Right Overseer of the Marshalate, and the campaign troops under his command were rewarded with gifts in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter Jinshan County was elevated to Zhen Prefecture. Gaoqi was made defense commissioner and acting right overseer of the marshalate, and the campaign troops under his command were rewarded according to merit.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年八月，尚書左丞完顏綱將兵十萬行省於縉山，敗績。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhiyong, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wanyan Gang led one hundred thousand troops on provincial duty at Jinshan and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of the Zhiyong era, Left Vice Director Wanyan Gang led one hundred thousand troops on provincial duty at Jinshan and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，遷元帥右監軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was transferred to Right Army Overseer of the Marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyou era he was promoted to right army overseer of the marshalate.

sentences.zh: 閏月，詔高琪曰：「聞軍事皆中覆，得無失機會乎？

translations.literal: In the intercalary month an edict told Gaoqi: "I hear that all military affairs are reported upward for approval—might opportunities not be lost?
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month an edict told Gaoqi, "I hear that all military matters require central approval. Are opportunities not being lost?

sentences.zh: 自今當即行之，朕但責成功耳。」

translations.literal: From now on you should act at once; I only hold you responsible for success."
translations.idiomatic: From now on act at once. I hold you responsible only for results."

sentences.zh: 是月，被詔自鎮州移軍守禦中都迤南，次良鄉不得前，乃還中都。

translations.literal: That month, by edict he moved his army from Zhen Prefecture to defend south of the Central Capital; he halted at Liangxiang and could not advance, then returned to the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That month he was ordered to move his army from Zhen Prefecture to defend the approaches south of the Central Capital. He halted at Liangxiang, could not advance, and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 每出戰輒敗，紇石烈執中戒之曰：「汝連敗矣，若再不勝，當以軍法從事。」

translations.literal: Each time he went out to battle he was defeated. Heshilie Zhizhong warned him: "You have suffered repeated defeats; if you do not win again, military law will be applied."
translations.idiomatic: Each time he took the field he was defeated. Wanyan Heshilie Zhizhong warned him, "You have lost battle after battle. If you fail again, you will face military law."

sentences.zh: 及出，果敗，高琪懼誅。

translations.literal: When he went out, he was indeed defeated, and Gaoqi feared execution.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out again, he was indeed defeated, and Gaoqi feared execution.

sentences.zh: 十月辛亥，高琪自軍中入，遂以兵圍執中第，殺執中，持其首詣闕待罪。

translations.literal: On xinhai of the tenth month, Gaoqi entered from the army, then with troops surrounded Zhizhong's residence, killed Zhizhong, and bearing his head went to the palace gate to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the tenth month, Gaoqi entered the capital from camp, surrounded Zhizhong's residence with troops, killed him, and presented his head at the palace gate to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 宣宗赦之，以為左副元帥，一行將士遷賞有差。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong pardoned him and made him Left Vice Marshal; the officers and soldiers of his column were promoted and rewarded in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong pardoned him and appointed him left vice marshal. The officers and soldiers who had accompanied him were promoted and rewarded according to merit.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔曰：「胡沙虎畜無君之心，形跡露見，不可盡言。

translations.literal: On bingyin an edict said: "Hu Shahu harbored a heart without regard for his lord; his traces were exposed and visible—it cannot all be told.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day an edict declared: "Hu Shahu harbored treasonous intent, and his conduct had become all too plain to recount in full.

sentences.zh: 武衛副使提點近侍局慶山奴、近侍局使斜烈、直長撒合輦累曾陳奏，方慎圖之。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Martial Guard and Intendant of the Inner Service Bureau Qingshan Nu, Commissioner of the Inner Service Bureau Xielie, and Direct Attendant Sahelian had repeatedly memorialized; we were only then carefully plotting against him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Qingshan Nu of the Martial Guard and intendant of the Inner Service Bureau, Commissioner Xielie of the Inner Service Bureau, and direct attendant Sahelian had repeatedly memorialized against him, and we were carefully planning action.

sentences.zh: 斜烈漏此意于按察判官胡魯，胡魯以告翰林待制訛出，訛出達于高琪，今月十五日將胡沙虎戮訖。

translations.literal: Xielie leaked this intent to Investigation Commissioner Adjunct Judge Hulu; Hulu told Hanlin Attendant Echu; Echu reached Gaoqi—and on the fifteenth of this month Hu Shahu was executed to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie disclosed this plan to investigation commissioner adjunct judge Hulu, who informed Hanlin attendant Echu, who in turn informed Gaoqi. On the fifteenth of this month Hu Shahu was put to death.

sentences.zh: 惟茲臣庶將恐有疑，肆降劄書，不匿厥旨。」

translations.literal: Only lest officials and commoners here should fear doubt, we broadly issue this sealed letter and do not conceal its intent."
translations.idiomatic: Lest officials and commoners harbor doubts, we issue this edict openly and conceal nothing of its purpose."

sentences.zh: 論者謂高琪專殺，故降此詔。

translations.literal: Commentators say that because Gaoqi killed on his own authority, this edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that because Gaoqi had carried out the killing on his own authority, this edict was issued to justify it.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜平章政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was appointed grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 宣宗論馬政，顧高琪曰：「往歲市馬西夏，今肯市否？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong discussed horse administration and turned to Gaoqi: "In past years we bought horses from Western Xia—will they sell now?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong discussed horse policy and turned to Gaoqi. "In past years we purchased horses from Western Xia. Will they sell to us now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「木波畜馬甚多，市之可得，括緣邊部落馬，亦不少矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Mubo keeps very many horses; by purchase they may be obtained, and by registering horses of frontier tribes along the border, there are also not a few."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Mubo keeps a great many horses and would sell them if approached. Horses may also be requisitioned from the frontier tribes, and these would not be few."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「盡括邊馬，緩急如之何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If all frontier horses are registered, what of urgency?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If all frontier horses are requisitioned, what will we do in an emergency?"

sentences.zh: 閱三日，複奏曰：「河南鎮防二十余軍，計可得精騎二萬，緩急亦足用。」

translations.literal: After three days he memorialized again: "The more than twenty garrison-defense armies of Henan—counting them, elite cavalry of twenty thousand may be obtained; in urgency this is also sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he memorialized again: "The more than twenty garrison armies of Henan could furnish some twenty thousand elite cavalry, which would suffice even in an emergency."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「馬雖多，養之有法，習之有時，詳諭所司令加意也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Though horses be many, there is method in raising them and season in training them—instruct the offices in detail to give this special attention."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "However many the horses, there is a proper way to raise them and a proper season to train them. Instruct the responsible offices to give this their utmost attention."

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年十一月，宣宗問高琪曰：「所造軍器往往不可用，此誰之罪也？」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Zhenyou, Emperor Xuanzong asked Gaoqi: "The weapons manufactured are often unusable—whose fault is this?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of the Zhenyou era, Emperor Xuanzong asked Gaoqi, "The weapons we manufacture are often unusable. Whose fault is this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「軍器美惡在兵部，材物則戶部，工匠則工部。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Whether arms are fine or poor lies with the Ministry of War; materials lie with the Ministry of Revenue; craftsmen lie with the Ministry of Works."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The quality of arms lies with the Ministry of War, the materials with the Ministry of Revenue, and the craftsmen with the Ministry of Works."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「治之！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Correct it!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Correct it!

sentences.zh: 且將敗事。」

translations.literal: It will soon ruin affairs."
translations.idiomatic: It will soon ruin our affairs."

sentences.zh: 宣宗問楊安兒事，高琪對曰：「賊方據險，臣令主將以石牆圍之，勢不得出，擒在旦夕矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked about Yang An'er; Gaoqi replied: "The bandit now holds rugged ground; your subject ordered the chief commander to wall him in with stone ramparts—he cannot get out by force; capture is within a day or two."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about Yang An'er. Gaoqi replied, "The rebel holds rugged terrain. I have ordered the chief commander to wall him in with stone ramparts. He cannot escape, and capture is only a matter of days."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「可以急攻，或力戰突圍，我師必有傷者。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You may press the attack, but if he fights fiercely to break out, our army is sure to suffer casualties."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Press the attack if you will, but if he fights fiercely to break out, our troops are sure to suffer casualties."

sentences.zh: 應奉翰林文字完顏素蘭自中都議軍事還，上書求見，乞屏左右。

translations.literal: Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting Wanyan Sulan, returning from discussing military affairs at the Central Capital, memorialized requesting audience and begged to dismiss those at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin attendant Wanyan Sulan, returning from military consultations at the Central Capital, submitted a memorial requesting an audience and asked that attendants be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 故事，有奏密事輒屏左右。

translations.literal: By precedent, when one memorializes a secret matter attendants at left and right are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a confidential matter was reported, attendants were dismissed from the audience.

sentences.zh: 先是，太府監丞游茂以高琪威權太重，中外畏之，常以為憂，因入見，屏人密奏，請裁抑之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse You Mao, because Gaoqi's authority and power were too heavy and court and countryside feared him, had often taken this as a worry; therefore on entering audience he dismissed others and secretly memorialized, asking to curb and restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Vice Director You Mao of the Imperial Storehouse, troubled that Gaoqi's power had grown too great and that court and country alike feared him, had requested a private audience and secretly memorialized that Gaoqi's authority should be curtailed.

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「既委任之，權安得不重？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "Since he has been entrusted, how can his power not be heavy?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong said, "Since I have entrusted him with office, how can his authority fail to be weighty?"

sentences.zh: 茂退不自安，複欲結高琪，詣其第上書曰：「宰相自有體，豈可以此生人主之疑，招天下之議。」

translations.literal: Mao withdrew, ill at ease; he again wished to win Gaoqi over, went to his residence and submitted a letter saying: "A chief councilor has his own proper form—how can one by this arouse the lord's suspicion and invite criticism from all under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Mao withdrew uneasy, then sought to win Gaoqi over instead. He went to his residence and submitted a letter: "A chief councilor must observe proper dignity. How can you act in ways that arouse the sovereign's suspicion and invite criticism throughout the realm?"

sentences.zh: 恐高琪不相信，複曰：「茂嘗間見主上，實惡相公權重。

translations.literal: Fearing Gaoqi would not believe him, he added: "Mao once had a private audience with the lord and truly dislikes the Chancellor's heavy power.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Gaoqi would not trust him, he added, "I once had a private audience with the emperor and know that he truly resents your excessive power.

sentences.zh: 相公若能用茂，當使上不疑，而下無所議。」

translations.literal: If the Chancellor can employ Mao, he will make the sovereign free of doubt and those below without criticism."
translations.idiomatic: If you will employ me, I can remove the emperor's suspicions and silence criticism below."

sentences.zh: 高琪聞茂嘗請間屏人奏事，疑之，乃具以聞。

translations.literal: Gaoqi, hearing that Mao had once requested a private audience with attendants dismissed to memorialize, suspected him and reported the whole matter.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi, learning that Mao had once requested a private audience to report against him, grew suspicious and reported the entire affair to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遊茂論死，詔免死，杖一百，除名。

translations.literal: You Mao was sentenced to death by discussion; an edict spared his life, gave him one hundred blows with the staff, and removed his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: You Mao was condemned to death, but an edict commuted the sentence to one hundred strokes of the staff and removal from office.

sentences.zh: 自是凡屏人奏事，必令近臣一人侍立。

translations.literal: From this time forth, whenever anyone memorialized with attendants dismissed, one close attendant was always ordered to stand in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever a confidential memorial was presented, the emperor ordered one close attendant to remain standing by.

sentences.zh: 及素蘭請密，召至近侍局，給筆劄，使書所欲言。

translations.literal: When Sulan requested secrecy, he was summoned to the Bureau of Close Attendance, given brush and paper, and made to write what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: When Sulan requested a private audience, he was summoned to the Bureau of Close Attendance, furnished with brush and paper, and told to write out everything he wished to say.

sentences.zh: 少頃，宣宗禦便殿見之，惟留近侍局直長趙和和侍立。

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Xuanzong received him in the side hall of the inner palace; only Zhao Hehe, chief registrar of the Bureau of Close Attendance, was kept to stand in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Emperor Xuanzong received him in a side hall of the inner palace, keeping only Zhao Hehe, chief registrar of the Bureau of Close Attendance, in attendance.

sentences.zh: 素蘭奏曰：「日者元帥府議削伯德文哥兵權，朝廷乃詔領義軍。

translations.literal: Sulan memorialized saying: "Recently the Marshalate discussed reducing Bode Wenge's military authority; the court thereupon ordered him to command the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: Sulan said, "Recently the marshalate proposed stripping Bode Wenge of military authority, whereupon the court ordered him to command the loyalist armies instead.

sentences.zh: 改除之命拒而不受，元帥府方欲討捕，朝廷複赦之，且不令隸元帥府。

translations.literal: He refused the appointment order of transfer; the marshalate was about to pursue and capture him, but the court again pardoned him and moreover did not allow him to be subordinate to the marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the new appointment. The marshalate was preparing to arrest him when the court pardoned him again and moreover exempted him from marshalate authority.

sentences.zh: 不知誰為陛下畫此計者，臣自外風聞皆出平章高琪。」

translations.literal: I do not know who drew up this plan for Your Majesty; from outside I hear by rumor that it all came from Grand Councilor Gaoqi."
translations.idiomatic: I do not know who devised this policy for Your Majesty, but rumor from outside the court traces it all to Grand Councilor Gaoqi."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「汝何以知此事出於高琪？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "How do you know this affair came from Gaoqi?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How do you know this affair originated with Gaoqi?"

sentences.zh: 素蘭曰：「臣見文哥與永清副提控劉溫牒雲，差人張希韓至自南京，道副樞平章處分，已奏令文哥隸大名行省，毋遵中都帥府約束。

translations.literal: Sulan said: "Your subject saw a dispatch from Wenge to Liu Wen, deputy commander of Yongqing, saying that an envoy Zhang Xihan arrived from Nanjing stating the disposition of the Vice Marshal Grand Councilor, already memorialized ordering Wenge subordinate to the Daming Branch Secretariat, not to follow the Central Capital marshalate's directives.
translations.idiomatic: Sulan said, "I have seen a dispatch from Wenge to Liu Wen, deputy commander of Yongqing, stating that an envoy named Zhang Xihan arrived from Nanjing bearing orders from the vice marshal of state. It had already been reported that Wenge was placed under the Daming Branch Secretariat and was no longer subject to the Central Capital marshalate.

sentences.zh: 溫即具言于帥府。

translations.literal: Wen immediately reported the whole affair to the marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wen reported the matter in full to the marshalate.

sentences.zh: 然則文哥與高琪計結，明矣。」

translations.literal: Thus Wenge and Gaoqi have plotted together—this is clear."
translations.idiomatic: It is plain, then, that Wenge and Gaoqi are in league."

sentences.zh: 上頷之。

translations.literal: The sovereign nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 素蘭複奏曰：「高琪本無勳望，向以畏死擅殺胡沙虎，計出於無聊耳。

translations.literal: Sulan again memorialized: "Gaoqi originally had no distinguished merit; formerly out of fear of death he presumptuously killed Hushahu—the plan came from desperation alone.
translations.idiomatic: Sulan went on, "Gaoqi never earned distinction. He killed Hushahu out of sheer terror for his own life—a desperate man's expedient, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 妒賢能，樹黨與，竊弄威權，自作威福。

translations.literal: He is jealous of talent and ability, establishes factions, usurps and manipulates authority and power, and makes authority and favor for himself alone.
translations.idiomatic: He envies the capable, builds factions, usurps authority, and treats the realm's power as his private possession.

sentences.zh: 去歲，都下書生樊知一詣高琪，言颭軍不可信，恐生亂。

translations.literal: Last year the capital student Fan Zhiyi went to Gaoqi and said the campaign troops were untrustworthy and might stir disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Last year a scholar of the capital named Fan Zhiyi went to Gaoqi and warned that the campaign troops were unreliable and might provoke rebellion.

sentences.zh: 高琪以刀杖決殺之，自是無複敢言軍國利害者。

translations.literal: Gaoqi had him beaten to death with blades and staves; from this time none again dared speak of matters affecting army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi had him beaten to death with blades and staves. After that no one dared speak frankly about the welfare of army and state.

sentences.zh: 使其黨移剌塔不也為武甯軍節度使，招颭軍，已而無功，複以為武衛軍使。

translations.literal: He caused his partisan Yila Tabuye to be made military commissioner of Wuning Army, to recruit campaign troops; before long without success, he was again made commander of the Martial Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his partisan Yila Tabuye as military commissioner of the Wuning Army to recruit the campaign troops. When this failed, Tabuye was made commander of the Martial Guard instead.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，此賊滅亂紀綱，戕害忠良，實有不欲國家平治之意。

translations.literal: In your subject's view, this villain destroys order and law, slays the loyal and good, and truly has no wish for the state's peace and good government.
translations.idiomatic: In my judgment this traitor destroys order, destroys the loyal, and plainly does not wish the state well.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下斷然行之，社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty acts decisively will it be the fortune of the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty acts decisively will the altars of state be blessed."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「朕徐思之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "We shall think on this slowly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I shall consider this carefully."

sentences.zh: 素蘭出，複戒曰：「慎無泄也。」

translations.literal: Sulan withdrew, and was again admonished: "Take care—do not leak this."
translations.idiomatic: Sulan withdrew, and was again warned: "Take care not to breathe a word of this."

sentences.zh: 四年十月，大元大兵取潼關，次嵩、汝間，待闕台院令史高嶷上書曰：「向者河朔敗績，朝廷不時出應，此失機會一也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year, the Great Yuan's great army took Tong Pass and halted between Song and Ru; Acting Clerk Gao Yi of the Daitaiyuan submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly in the defeat in Heshuo, the court did not respond in season—this is the first lost opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year, the Mongol armies took Tong Pass and camped between Song and Ru. Gao Yi, a clerk of the Daitaiyuan, submitted a memorial: "When our armies were routed in Heshuo, the court failed to respond in time. That was the first lost opportunity.

sentences.zh: 及深入吾境，都城精兵無慮數十萬，若效命一戰，必無今日之憂，此失機會二也。

translations.literal: When they penetrated deep into our territory, the capital's crack troops were surely several hundred thousand; if they had devoted their lives to one battle, today's worries would certainly not exist—this is the second lost opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy penetrated deep into our territory, the capital had several hundred thousand elite troops. Had they been sent into a decisive battle, we would not face today's peril. That was the second lost opportunity.

sentences.zh: 既退之後，不議追襲，此失機會三也。

translations.literal: After the enemy withdrew, no pursuit was discussed—this is the third lost opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew, no pursuit was even discussed. That was the third lost opportunity.

sentences.zh: 今已度關，不亟進禦，患益深矣。

translations.literal: Now they have already crossed the pass; if we do not hasten to advance and resist, the disaster grows deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have crossed the pass. If we do not hurry to meet them in battle, disaster will only deepen.

sentences.zh: 乞命平章政事高琪為帥，以厭眾心。」

translations.literal: I beg that Grand Councilor Gaoqi be ordered as commander, to satisfy the hearts of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Grand Councilor Gaoqi be appointed commander in chief to satisfy the people's expectations."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 禦史台言：「兵逾潼關、崤、澠，深入重地，近抵西郊。

translations.literal: The Censorate said: "Troops have crossed Tong Pass, Xiao, and Mian, penetrated into crucial territory, and drawn near the western suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate reported, "Enemy troops have crossed Tong Pass, Xiao, and Mian, penetrated deep into our heartland, and drawn near the western suburbs of the capital.

sentences.zh: 彼知京師屯宿重兵，不復叩城索戰，但以遊騎遮絕道路，而別兵攻擊州縣，是亦困京師之漸也。

translations.literal: They know the capital garrisons heavy troops and no longer knock at the walls demanding battle, but only use roaming cavalry to cut off roads while separate troops attack prefectures and counties—this too is the gradual method of besieging the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the capital holds a massive garrison, they no longer assault the walls but send raiding cavalry to sever the roads while other columns attack prefectures and counties. This too is their strategy for gradually strangling the capital.

sentences.zh: 若專以城守為事，中都之危又將見於今日，況公私蓄積視中都百不及一，此臣等所為寒心也。

translations.literal: If we devote ourselves solely to wall defense, the danger to the Central Capital will again appear today; moreover public and private stores compared with the Central Capital are not one in a hundred—this is what makes your subjects' hearts cold.
translations.idiomatic: If we rely solely on defending the walls, the capital will suffer the same fate Zhongdu once did. And the stores of Nanjing, public and private alike, are not one percent of what Zhongdu held. This is what chills our hearts.

sentences.zh: 不攻京城而縱其別攻州縣，是猶火在腹心，撥置於手足之上，均一身也，願陛下察之。

translations.literal: Not attacking the capital city but letting separate forces attack prefectures and counties is like fire in the belly and heart while attending to the arms and legs—they are one body alike; I beg Your Majesty to consider this.
translations.idiomatic: To let the enemy ravage the provinces while we hold the walls is like tending a wounded limb while fire rages in the belly. The realm is one body. I beg Your Majesty to see this.

sentences.zh: 請以陝西兵扼拒潼關，與右副元帥蒲察阿裏不孫為掎角之勢，選在京勇敢之將十數人，各付精兵數千，隨宜伺察，且戰且守，複諭河北，亦以此待之。」

translations.literal: I request that Shaanxi troops hold and block Tong Pass, forming pincer coordination with Right Vice Marshal Puxian Ali Busun; select a dozen or so bold generals in the capital, each given several thousand elite troops, to watch and act as circumstances require, fighting while defending; instruct Hebei as well to await them in this way."
translations.idiomatic: Let Shaanxi troops hold Tong Pass in coordination with Right Vice Marshal Puxian Ali Busun. Select a dozen bold commanders in the capital, give each several thousand elite troops, and let them probe the enemy and fight as circumstances demand. Send the same orders to Hebei."

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書省，高琪奏曰：「台官素不習兵，備禦方略，非所知也。」

translations.literal: An edict referred the matter to the Ministry of State Affairs; Gaoqi memorialized: "Censorate officials by nature do not practice warfare—defense strategies are not what they know."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of State Affairs. Gaoqi replied, "Censorate officials know nothing of military affairs. Defense strategy is not their province."

sentences.zh: 遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: And there the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 高琪止欲以重兵屯駐南京以自固，州郡殘破不復恤也。

translations.literal: Gaoqi only wished to mass heavy troops garrisoned at Nanjing to secure himself; devastated prefectures and counties he no longer cared for.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi cared only to mass troops at Nanjing for his own security and gave no thought to devastated provinces.

sentences.zh: 宣宗惑之，計行言聽，終以自斃。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was deluded; plans he advanced were heard and followed, and in the end he brought about his own destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deluded by him, followed his every counsel, and in the end was destroyed by his own minister.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進拜尚書右丞相，奏曰：「凡監察有失糾彈者從本法。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced and appointed Right Chief Minister of the Ministry of State Affairs; he memorialized: "Whenever surveillance officials fail in impeachment and scrutiny, let the original law apply.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to right chief minister of the Ministry of State Affairs and memorialized, "Whenever surveillance officials fail to impeach offenses properly, the statute shall apply as written.

sentences.zh: 若人使入國，私通言語，說知本國事情，宿衛、近侍官、承應人出入親王、公主、宰執之家，災傷闕食，體究不實，致傷人命，轉運軍儲，而有私載，及考試舉人關防不嚴者，並的杖。

translations.literal: If envoys enter the realm and privately communicate words, informing them of this state's affairs; if guards of the night watch, close-attendance officials, and attendants enter the houses of imperial princes, princesses, and chief ministers; if disaster and famine leave people without food and investigation is not truthful, causing injury to human life; if military stores are transported with private loads aboard; and if examination of candidates and border controls at gates are not strict—all shall receive corporal punishment by designated staff.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover: envoys who converse privately and reveal state secrets; palace guards and attendants who visit princes, princesses, or chief ministers; officials who falsify famine relief investigations with fatal consequences; logistics officers who carry private cargo; examiners who fail to enforce security—all shall receive corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 在京犯至兩次者，台官減監察一等論贖，餘止坐專差者。

translations.literal: Those who offend in the capital up to two times: censorate officials lose one rank of surveillance in discussing ransom, the rest are punished only in the specialized assignment.
translations.idiomatic: For a second offense in the capital, censorate officials lose one grade in their performance review; others are punished only within their assigned jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 任滿日議定升降。

translations.literal: On the day their term ends their promotion or demotion is decided by discussion.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of term their promotion or demotion shall be determined accordingly.

sentences.zh: 若任內有漏察之事應的決者，依格雖為稱職，止從平常，平常者從降罰。」

translations.literal: If within their term there are matters that were not surveilled which should have received corporal judgment, though by regulation they are rated competent, they are rated only ordinary; those rated ordinary are demoted in penalty."
translations.idiomatic: If during their term they fail to impeach an offense requiring corporal punishment, they shall be rated merely satisfactory even if otherwise competent, and a merely satisfactory rating entails demotion."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations were approved.

sentences.zh: 高琪請修南京裏城，宣宗曰：「此役一興，民滋病矣。

translations.literal: Gaoqi requested repairing the inner wall of Nanjing; Emperor Xuanzong said: "Once this labor is raised, the people suffer more sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi proposed repairing the inner wall of Nanjing. The emperor said, "Once this work begins, the people will suffer all the more.

sentences.zh: 城雖完固，能獨安乎？」

translations.literal: Though the walls be complete and strong, can we alone be secure?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if the walls are strong, can they alone keep us secure?"

sentences.zh: 興定元年十月，右司諫許古勸宣宗與宋議和，宣宗命古草牒，以示宰臣，高琪曰：「辭有哀祈之意，自示微弱不足取。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Xingding, Right Department Remonstrator Xu Gu urged Emperor Xuanzong to negotiate peace with Song; the emperor ordered Gu to draft a document and show it to the chief ministers; Gaoqi said: "The wording bears pleading and supplication—by itself showing weakness unworthy of acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Xingding, Right Department Remonstrator Xu Gu urged the emperor to negotiate peace with Song. The emperor ordered Xu to draft a document and show it to the chief ministers. Gaoqi objected, "The language is pleading and abject. It shows weakness and will gain us nothing.

sentences.zh: 遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 集賢院諮議官呂鑒言：「南邊屯兵數十萬，自唐、鄧至壽、泗沿邊居民逃亡殆盡，兵士亦多亡者，亦以人煙絕少故也。

translations.literal: Advisory Official Lü Jian of the Academy of Assembled Talents said: "On the southern frontier several hundred thousand troops are garrisoned; from Tang and Deng to Shou and Si along the border the inhabitants have fled almost entirely, and soldiers too have many deserters—this too is because human habitation is nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: Advisory official Lü Jian of the Academy of Assembled Talents said, "We have several hundred thousand troops on the southern frontier. From Tang and Deng to Shou and Si the border population has fled almost entirely, and many soldiers have deserted as well, because the land is nearly empty.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗比監息州榷場，每場所獲布帛數千匹、銀數百兩，大計布帛數萬匹，銀數千兩，兵興以來俱失之矣。

translations.literal: Your subject once concurrently supervised the Xizhou tax market; each session obtained several thousand bolts of cloth and several hundred taels of silver—in the gross tens of thousands of bolts and thousands of taels; since warfare arose all have been lost.
translations.idiomatic: I once supervised the Xizhou trade market. Each session yielded several thousand bolts of cloth and several hundred taels of silver—tens of thousands of bolts and thousands of taels in all. Since the war began we have lost all of this revenue.

sentences.zh: 夫軍民有逃亡之病，而國家失日獲之利，非計也。

translations.literal: Now army and people have the affliction of flight, yet the state loses profit gained daily—not a plan.
translations.idiomatic: To suffer mass desertion among troops and civilians while forfeiting daily revenue is no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 今隆冬冱寒，吾騎得騁，當重兵屯境上，馳書諭之，誠為大便。

translations.literal: Now in deep winter with bitter cold, our cavalry can run free; we should mass heavy troops on the border, send swift letters to instruct them—this is truly great convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Deep winter favors our cavalry. Mass troops on the border and send an urgent dispatch. The opportunity is ripe.

sentences.zh: 若俟春和，則利在於彼，難與議矣。

translations.literal: If we wait until spring is mild, the advantage lies with them and negotiation becomes hard.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until spring, and the advantage passes to them. Negotiation will then be far harder.

sentences.zh: 昔燕人獲趙王，趙遣辯士說之，不許，一牧豎請行，趙王乃還。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yan captured the King of Zhao; Zhao sent debaters to persuade them—no permission; one shepherd boy requested to go, and the King of Zhao was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Yan held the king of Zhao prisoner, Zhao sent eloquent envoys who failed to win his release. A shepherd boy volunteered, and the king was returned.

sentences.zh: 孔子失馬，馭卒得之。

translations.literal: Confucius lost a horse; a carriage driver recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius lost his horse; a groom found it.

sentences.zh: 人無貴賤，苟中事機，皆可以成功。

translations.literal: Among men there is no noble or base—if one hits the turning point of affairs, all can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Rank means nothing. Whoever grasps the moment can succeed.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不肖，願效牧豎馭卒之智，伏望宸斷。」

translations.literal: Though your subject is unworthy, he wishes to emulate the shepherd boy and carriage driver in wisdom; he bows his forehead awaiting the sovereign's decision."
translations.idiomatic: Humble though I am, I would emulate that shepherd and that groom. I beg Your Majesty's judgment."

sentences.zh: 詔問尚書省。

translations.literal: An edict asked the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高琪曰：「鑒狂妄無稽，但其氣岸可尚，宜付陝西行省備任使。」

translations.literal: Gaoqi said: "Jian is arrogant and without basis, but his spirited bearing is admirable—he should be sent to the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat to await assignment."
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi said, "Jian is arrogant and reckless, but he has spirit. Assign him to the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat for whatever duty may arise."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 十二月，胥鼎諫伐宋，語在鼎傳。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xu Ding remonstrated against attacking Song—the account is in Ding's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xu Ding remonstrated against the campaign against Song. His words are recorded in his biography.

sentences.zh: 高琪曰：「大軍已進，無複可議。」

translations.literal: Gaoqi said: "The great army has already advanced—there is nothing more to discuss."
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi said, "The main army has already advanced. The matter is not open to debate."

sentences.zh: 遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: And there it ended.

sentences.zh: 二年，胥鼎上書諫曰：「錢谷之冗，非九重所能兼，天子總大綱，責成功而已。」

translations.literal: In the second year, Xu Ding submitted a memorial remonstrating: "The glut of finance and grain is not what the Ninefold Heights can encompass together; the Son of Heaven holds the great outline and demands success—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Xu Ding memorialized, "The burden of finance and grain is more than the throne can supervise in detail. The Son of Heaven holds the great outline and demands results—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 高琪曰：「陛下法上天行健之義，憂勤庶務，夙夜不遑，乃太平之階也。

translations.literal: Gaoqi said: "Your Majesty follows Heaven's meaning of the vigorous moving—concerned and diligent in all affairs, from dawn to night without leisure—this is the stairway to great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi said, "Your Majesty emulates Heaven's vigor, laboring over every affair from dawn till night without rest. That is the path to peace.

sentences.zh: 鼎言非是。」

translations.literal: Ding's words are not correct."
translations.idiomatic: Xu's counsel is mistaken."

sentences.zh: 宣宗以南北用兵，深以為憂，右司諫呂造上章：「乞詔內外百官各上封事，直言無諱。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, because troops were used north and south, was deeply worried; Right Department Remonstrator Lü Zao submitted a memorial: "I beg an edict that inner and outer officials each submit sealed reports, speaking straight without taboo.
translations.idiomatic: With war on both fronts the emperor was deeply troubled. Right Department Remonstrator Lü Zao memorialized, "I beg that inner and outer officials be ordered to submit sealed memorials and speak without reserve.

sentences.zh: 或時召見，親為訪問。

translations.literal: Or at times summon them to audience and personally inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Summon them for audience when needed and question them yourself.

sentences.zh: 陛下博采兼聽，以盡群下之情，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty broadly gathers and jointly hears, to exhaust the feelings of all below—great fortune for all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty listens broadly and weighs every counsel, you will know the mind of the realm. The realm would be blessed indeed."

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉納，詔集百官議河北、陝西守禦之策。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong praised and accepted; an edict gathered officials to discuss strategies for defending Hebei and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered officials to assemble and deliberate on the defense of Hebei and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 高琪心忌之，不用一言。

translations.literal: Gaoqi resented this in his heart and used not a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi resented this and suppressed every proposal.

sentences.zh: 是時，築汴京城裏城，宣宗問高琪曰：「人言此役恐不能就，如何？」

translations.literal: At this time the inner wall of Bianjing was being built; Emperor Xuanzong asked Gaoqi: "Men say this labor may not be completed—how is it?"
translations.idiomatic: At this time the inner wall of Bianjing was under construction. The emperor asked Gaoqi, "Some say this project may never be finished. What do you say?"

sentences.zh: 高琪曰：「終當告成，但其濠未及浚耳。」

translations.literal: Gaoqi said: "In the end it will be reported complete, but its moat has not yet been dredged."
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi said, "It will be completed in the end, though the moat has not yet been dug."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「無濠可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can we do without a moat?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Can we manage without a moat?"

sentences.zh: 高琪曰：「苟防城有法，正使兵來，臣等愈得效力。」

translations.literal: Gaoqi said: "If city defense has method, even should troops come, your subjects will the more be able to exert their strength."
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi said, "If the defenses are sound, even when the enemy comes we ministers can serve all the better."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「與其臨城，曷若不令至此為善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Rather than face them at the walls, how is it not better not to let them reach here?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Better to keep the enemy from reaching the walls at all than to meet them there."

sentences.zh: 高琪無以對。

translations.literal: Gaoqi had nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi had no answer.

sentences.zh: 高琪自為宰相，專固權寵，擅作威福，與高汝礪相唱和。

translations.literal: From the time Gaoqi became chief minister, he monopolized power and favor, presumptuously made authority and favor for himself, and echoed in concert with Gao Rulü.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaoqi became chief minister he monopolized power and favor, ruled by intimidation, and worked in concert with Gao Rulü.

sentences.zh: 高琪主機務，高汝礪掌利權，附己者用，不附己者斥。

translations.literal: Gaoqi presided over key affairs of state; Gao Rulü grasped the powers of profit; those who attached to them were employed, those who did not were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi controlled civil affairs while Gao Rulü controlled fiscal power. Those who attached themselves were promoted; those who refused were driven out.

sentences.zh: 凡言事忤意，及負材力或與己頡頑者，對宣宗陽稱其才，使幹當于河北，陰置之死地。

translations.literal: All who spoke on affairs contrary to his intent, and those bearing talent and strength or contending with him, he praised their ability before Emperor Xuanzong and sent them to manage affairs in Hebei, secretly placing them on ground of death.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who opposed him, or possessed talent enough to challenge him, he praised before the emperor and sent to Hebei on ostensibly important missions, secretly placing them in mortal peril.

sentences.zh: 自不兼樞密元帥之後，常欲得兵權，遂力勸宣宗伐宋。

translations.literal: Since he no longer held the concurrent posts of Privy Council and Marshal, he constantly wished to gain military authority and thus strenuously urged Emperor Xuanzong to attack Song.
translations.idiomatic: After losing his concurrent posts as privy councilor and marshal, he constantly sought military authority and tirelessly urged war against Song.

sentences.zh: 置河北不復為意，凡精兵皆置河南，苟且歲月，不肯輒出一卒，以應方面之急。

translations.literal: He no longer took Hebei to heart; all crack troops he placed in Henan, dragging out the months complacently, unwilling to send out a single soldier to answer urgent calls from the frontier circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned Hebei to its fate, massed all elite troops in Henan, and clung to complacency, refusing to dispatch a single soldier to relieve the frontier.

sentences.zh: 平章政事英王守純欲發其罪，密召右司員外郎王阿裏、知案蒲鮮石魯剌、令史蒲察胡魯謀之。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Prince of Ying Shouchun wished to expose his crimes; he secretly summoned Right Department Vice Director Wang Ali, Case Manager Puxian Shilula, and Clerk Pucha Hulu to plot.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor the Prince of Ying Shouchun wished to expose Gaoqi's crimes and secretly summoned Right Department Vice Director Wang Ali, case manager Puxian Shilula, and clerk Pucha Hulu to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 石魯剌、胡魯以告尚書省都事僕散奴失不，僕散奴失不以告高琪。

translations.literal: Shilula and Hulu told the Ministry of State Affairs Registrar Pusannushibu; Pusannushibu told Gaoqi.
translations.idiomatic: Shilula and Hulu informed the ministry registrar Pusannushibu, who reported the plot to Gaoqi.

sentences.zh: 英王懼高琪黨與，遂不敢發。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ying feared Gaoqi's faction and thus did not dare expose it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ying, fearing Gaoqi's faction, did not dare proceed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，高琪使奴賽不殺其妻，乃歸罪於賽不，送開封府殺之以滅口。

translations.literal: Before long Gaoqi had his slave Saibu kill his wife, then attributed guilt to Saibu and sent him to Kaifeng Prefecture to be killed to silence the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gaoqi had his slave Saibu kill his wife, then blamed Saibu and sent him to Kaifeng Prefecture for execution to silence witnesses.

sentences.zh: 開封府畏高琪，不敢發其實，賽不論死。

translations.literal: Kaifeng Prefecture feared Gaoqi and did not dare expose the truth; Saibu was sentenced to death by discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng Prefecture, fearing Gaoqi, concealed the truth, and Saibu was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 事覺，宣宗久聞高琪奸惡，遂因此事誅之，時興定三年十二月也。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Emperor Xuanzong had long heard of Gaoqi's treachery and evil and thus on this account executed him—it was the twelfth month of the third year of Xingding.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, the emperor, who had long known of Gaoqi's wickedness, used it as grounds to execute him. It was the twelfth month of the third year of Xingding.

sentences.zh: 尚書省都事僕散奴失不以英王謀告高琪，論死。

translations.literal: Ministry Registrar Pusannushibu, for not reporting the Prince of Ying's plot to Gaoqi, was sentenced to death by discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry registrar Pusannushibu was condemned to death for failing to report the Prince of Ying's plot to Gaoqi.

sentences.zh: 蒲鮮石魯剌、蒲察胡魯各杖七十，勒停。

translations.literal: Puxian Shilula and Pucha Hulu each received seventy strokes of the staff and were ordered to cease office.
translations.idiomatic: Puxian Shilula and Pucha Hulu each received seventy strokes of the staff and were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗將遷南，欲置颭軍于平州，高琪難之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Xuanzong was about to move south, he wished to station campaign troops at Ping Prefecture; Gaoqi opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor planned to move south, he wished to station the campaign troops at Ping Prefecture. Gaoqi opposed the plan.

sentences.zh: 及遷汴，戒彖多厚撫此軍，彖多輒殺颭軍數人，以至於敗。

translations.literal: When the move to Bian was made, he admonished Tuo Duo to treat this army generously; Tuo Duo immediately killed several campaign troops, leading to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Bian he charged Tuo Duo to treat the army generously. Tuo Duo promptly executed several campaign soldiers, and the army was ruined.

sentences.zh: 宣宗末年嘗曰：「壞天下者，高琪、彖多也。」

translations.literal: In his later years Emperor Xuanzong once said: "Those who ruined all under Heaven were Gaoqi and Tuo Duo."
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor once said, "Those who ruined the realm were Gaoqi and Tuo Duo."

sentences.zh: 終身以為恨雲。

translations.literal: He bore this as regret to the end of his life, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He regretted it to the end of his days, it is said.

sentences.zh: 塔不也

translations.literal: Tabuye
translations.idiomatic: Yila Tabuye

sentences.zh: 移剌塔不也，東北路猛安人。

translations.literal: Yila Tabuye was a man of the Meng'an of the Northeast Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Tabuye came from a meng'an of the Northeast Circuit.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，累官西上閣門使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang, through successive offices he became Western Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Mingchang he rose through successive posts to Western Upper Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，襲父謀克。

translations.literal: In the second year he inherited his father's mohelen status.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he inherited his father's mohelen title.

sentences.zh: 泰和伐宋，有功，遙授同知慶州事，權迪列颭詳穩。

translations.literal: In the Taihe campaign against Song he had merit; he was appointed from afar as associate prefect of Qing Prefecture, acting tribal military overseer of the campaign forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe campaign against Song he distinguished himself and was appointed associate prefect of Qing Prefecture in absentia, with acting authority as tribal military overseer of the campaign troops.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複西北路招討判官，改尚輦局使、曹王傅。

translations.literal: On finishing mourning for his father he was recalled to serve as punitive-commissioner judge of the Northwest Circuit, then changed to Commissioner of the Imperial Chariot Bureau and Tutor to the Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: After observing mourning for his father he was recalled as punitive commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, then appointed commissioner of the Imperial Chariot Bureau and tutor to the Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，遷武甯軍節度使，招徠中都颭軍，無功，平章高琪芘之，召為武衛軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred as military commissioner of Wuning Army, to recruit the Central Capital's campaign troops—without success; Grand Councilor Gaoqi sheltered him and summoned him as commander-in-chief of the Martial Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he was made military commissioner of the Wuning Army to recruit the Central Capital campaign troops. When this failed, Grand Councilor Gaoqi protected him and had him appointed commander of the Martial Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 應奉翰林文字完顏素蘭嘗面奏高琪黨比，語在《高琪傳》。

translations.literal: Hanlin Attendant Wanyan Sulan once memorialized in audience on Gaoqi's factional partisanship—the account is in the "Biography of Gaoqi."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin attendant Wanyan Sulan once denounced Gaoqi's factionalism to the throne. The account appears in Gaoqi's biography.

sentences.zh: 尋知河南府事，兼副統軍，徙彰化軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was made administrator of Henan Prefecture, concurrently vice commander-in-chief; he was transferred as military commissioner of Zhanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed administrator of Henan Prefecture and vice commander-in-chief, then transferred to military commissioner of the Zhanghua Army.

sentences.zh: 上言：「盡籍山東、河間、大名猛安人為兵，老弱城守，壯者捍禦。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Register all the meng'an households of Shandong, Hejian, and Daming as soldiers; let the old and weak defend the cities and the strong resist the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial proposing that all meng'an households in Shandong, Hejian, and Daming be enrolled as soldiers, with the old and weak assigned to garrison the cities and the able-bodied men to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 又言：「河東地險人勇，步兵為天下冠，可盡調以戍諸隘。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The terrain of Hedong is perilous and its people brave; its infantry are foremost under Heaven and may all be transferred to garrison the passes."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Hedong's terrain was rugged and its people valiant, that its infantry were the finest in the realm, and that they should all be mobilized to garrison the strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 自是河東郡縣屯兵少，不可守矣。

translations.literal: From this time the garrison troops in the prefectures and counties of Hedong were few and could not be defended.
translations.idiomatic: From that point onward the prefectures and counties of Hedong were left with too few garrison troops to hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 改知臨洮府事，兼陝西副統軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Linzhou Prefecture and concurrently served as deputy commander-in-chief of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as prefect of Linzhou and concurrently served as deputy commander-in-chief in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年十一月，破夏兵於熟羊寨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Zhenyou he defeated Xia troops at Shuyang Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Zhenyou he routed Western Xia forces at Shuyang Stockade.

sentences.zh: 平章高琪率宰臣入賀曰：「塔不也以少敗眾，蓋陛下威德所致。」

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Gaoqi led the chief ministers in to congratulate him, saying: "Tabuye defeated the many with the few—surely this was brought about by Your Majesty's august authority and virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Gaoqi led the chief ministers in to offer congratulations, saying, "Tabuye defeated a larger force with fewer men—surely this reflects Your Majesty's august authority and virtue."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「自古興國皆賴忠賢，今茲立功，皆將率諸賢之力也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "Since antiquity every rising state has relied on loyal worthies; today's achievement rests on the strength of all our generals and worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong replied, "Since antiquity every rising state has relied on loyal worthies; the merit won today rests on the combined strength of our generals and worthy ministers."

sentences.zh: 乃以塔不也為勸農使，兼知平涼府事，進階銀青榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tabuye was appointed Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture and concurrently made administrator of Pingliang Prefecture, advancing in rank to Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Tabuye was then appointed commissioner for encouraging agriculture and concurrently made administrator of Pingliang Prefecture, with promotion to the rank of Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 四年，伐西夏，攻威、靈、安、會等州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he campaigned against Western Xia and attacked the prefectures of Wei, Ling, An, and Hui, among others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he campaigned against Western Xia and attacked Wei, Ling, An, Hui, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，知慶陽府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding he administered Qingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingding he was made administrator of Qingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷元帥左都監，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Left Overseer of the Marshalate and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to left overseer of the Marshalate and died in office.

sentences.zh: 論曰：高琪擅殺執中，宣宗不能正其罪，又曲為之說，以詔臣下。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Gaoqi killed Zhizhong on his own authority; Emperor Xuanzong could not rectify his crime but instead twisted the facts in an edict to his officials.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: When Gaoqi killed Zhizhong on his own authority, Emperor Xuanzong failed to punish the crime and instead twisted the facts in an edict to his officials.

sentences.zh: 就其事論之，人君欲誅大臣，而與近侍密謀于宮中，已非其道。

translations.literal: Judging the matter on its merits, when a ruler wishes to execute a great minister yet plots in secret with attendants inside the palace, the way is already wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Judged on its merits, when a ruler wishes to execute a great minister yet plots in secret with palace attendants, he has already departed from the proper way.

sentences.zh: 謀之不密，又為外臣所知，以告敗軍之將，因殺之以為說，此可欺後世邪？

translations.literal: The plot was not kept secret and was known to an outside official, who told a defeated general; he then killed him to provide an explanation—can this deceive later ages?
translations.idiomatic: The plot was not kept secret, an outside official learned of it and informed a defeated general, and the man was then killed to supply a cover story—can such a tale deceive posterity?

sentences.zh: 金至南渡，譬之尪羸病人，元氣無幾。

translations.literal: When Jin reached the southern transfer, it was like a wasted and feeble patient with scarcely any vital force left.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Jin moved its capital south, the dynasty was like a wasted patient with scarcely any vital force remaining.

sentences.zh: 琪喜吏而惡儒，好兵而厭靜，沮遷颭之議，破和宋之謀，正猶繆醫，投以烏喙、附子，只速其亡耳。

translations.literal: Gaoqi favored clerks and hated Confucians, loved arms and disliked quiet, obstructed the proposal to move the campaign troops, and shattered the plan to make peace with Song—just like a quack physician administering aconite and prepared aconite root, he only hastened its ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi favored clerks and despised Confucians, loved war and disdained peace, blocked the plan to relocate the campaign troops, and wrecked the proposal to make peace with Song—like a quack physician dosing a dying man with aconite and prepared aconite, he only hastened the dynasty's collapse.

sentences.zh: 使宣宗於擅殺之日，即能伸大義而誅之，何至誤國如是邪。

translations.literal: Had Emperor Xuanzong, on the day of the unauthorized killing, been able to uphold great righteousness and execute him, how could he have misled the state to such a degree?
translations.idiomatic: Had Emperor Xuanzong upheld righteousness and executed Gaoqi on the day of that unauthorized killing, how could the state have been misled so disastrously?
